planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.3: By 2024, access, awareness and sustainable use of appropriate Resources, Assets,  Services and Markets by poor and rural producers, households, value-chain actors, and communities, including women and  youth improved.
planEntities.description:
Over 2,625 women smallholder farmers from 15 women-based farming cooperatives are demanding respect of their rights in community management of land for agriculture and their participation in the management of natural resources. 

These women smallholder farmers are demonstrating increased knowledge of, and ability to act on, their rights around agriculture, and land management. 

WFP:
WFP is providing climate smart agriculture training to 2,900 smallholder farmers including forest resource management, VSLA, and FFS. These farmers have access to market through the Home-Grown School Feeding Programme. WFP addresses PHL through the provision of 4 storage facilities and 8 agribusiness centers construction.

planEntities.name: Provide rural women, smallholder farmers with access to finance around food value chains
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.3: By 2024, access, awareness and sustainable use of appropriate Resources, Assets,  Services and Markets by poor and rural producers, households, value-chain actors, and communities, including women and  youth improved.
planEntities.description:
Over 40 Savings and Loans Associations are:
Breaking down barriers to finance – The associations are helping the women overcome common barriers, and access to finance has been one such barrier for many of them because there is a lack of limited or no formal financial institutions in their communities.
Empowering women to become changemakers – The women in the associations are investing in CSA and vegetable production because of loans taken from their respective SLAs. They have been able to make a profit. Also, the SLAs are not just about increasing income or serving as a social protection fund, they have also empowered the women to become active players in their various communities.
Promoting solidarity and equality – Being part of such successful community associations has led to inspiring gains in the women’s social status. They are starting their own businesses and are participating in community decision-making processes at the household and community levels. Being able to contribute financially within their families has even put the women on a more equal footing with their spouses.
Contributing to peace building – financial freedom for women from a combination of the SLAs and other businesses is enabling women to support peacebuilding efforts at the community level. 

WFP:
WFP is providing 65 smallholder farmer groups access to micro finance through the VSLA activities under the Integrated Food Security and PBF-Projects. 

UNDP Accelerated Community Development Programme (ACDP) support rural women smallholder farmers with access to finance around food value chains.

planEntities.name: Support efforts to scale up integrated HIV and TB treatment to reach the 95-95-95 Targets for People Living with HIV
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Capacity of national and sub-national institutions to provide quality, equitable, inclusive and decentralized social services is enhanced.
planEntities.description: UNICEF: A standout achievement in 2024 was the increase in the percentage of HIV-exposed infants receiving a virologic test within two months of birth. This figure rose from 76% in 2023 to 92.6% in 2024, reflecting a significant improvement in early diagnosis and treatment for these vulnerable infants. This increase highlights the success of targeted interventions to address mother-to-child transmission of HIV.

UNICEF: 150 adolescents (125 girls, 25 boys) in Montserrado, graduated from various vocational skills trainings including cosmetology, pastry making, tailoring, hotel management, and hospitality services.  1) Trained and equipped healthcare workers in four counties to conduct weekly integrated RMNCAH outreach services; Developed an advanced draft of the RMNCAH policy and the Child Strategy and Action Plan; developed a costed eMTCT Plan pending validation; Constructed a PSA oxygen plant in Bong County targeting over 571,960 women and children in six (6) counties to make oxygen readily available for RMNCAH and other emergencies. 2) supported data analysis and a deep dive into maternal mortality. 3) Provision of maternal health supplies to primary health care facilities in 7 counties of Grand Cape Mount, Grand Gedeh, Grand Kru, Gbarpolu, Grand Bassa, Montserrado, and Margibi; Inadequacy of supplies to all fifteen counties has been a major challenge and factor contributing to poor service provision and thus contributing to mortality and morbidity; as a result of this, mortality has been stagnant with no major changes. 4) Supported the reestablishment and strengthening of the Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR) at the national level.

planEntities.name: Empower women and girls in high burden counties including those living with HIV and AIDS with access to information, services, referral pathways, and economic empowerment opportunities
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Community leaders and members including vulnerable and marginalized group-members have the capacity to demand and utilize quality, equitable, decentralized, and age and gender-responsive essential social services
planEntities.description:
Over 100 community leaders, traditional leaders, and religious leaders from 36 communities are changing their perception of PLHIV and the association with SGBV. These leaders are increasingly engaged with implementing the SGBV referral pathway for PLHIV through their participation in ensuring that victims can access medical care, police, psychosocial care, safe homes, and the court. 

Almost 1,500 community members (females: 1,287; males: 209) and 1,412 urban and rural market women are wearing masks and engaged in social distancing and frequent handwashing to prevention COVID-19 infection. In addition, beneficiaries and communities are also cleaning and disinfecting their water and sanitation facilities. 

Misinformation about the coronavirus is being dismissed by the women and their communities. They are promoting all precautionary measures, especially hand washing and the wearing of masks as all beneficiaries gained access to over 14,500 locally produced stitch masks. 

Through the delivery of a comprehensive, sequenced ‘package’ of core interventions (e.g., literacy, numeracy, and business skills; access to finance, etc.) to empower beneficiaries economically and socially, some key results included: 

•	325 women and adolescent girls beneficiaries (those living with HIV/AIDS) in Montserrado, Bong, and Grand Bassa Counties are engaged in small businesses for income generation and better livelihood. They are organizing and managing their own businesses. Their market tables are being transformed into profitable businesses. 
•	Basic literacy and numeracy skills are building the confidence of beneficiaries and unleashing their full potential. 
•	325 beneficiaries are also now saving money as bank account holders while others have gained financial independence which has increased their participation in decision-making.
•	Some 26 local women beneficiaries are demonstrating their potential and resourcefulness as business program coaches and mentors for PLHIV. 
•	13 Savings and Loan Associations (SLAs) are providing financial security and independence for beneficiaries. These associations are offering sustainable, relevant solutions by adding value to a traditionally known and trusted model of saving. 
•	The financial independence gained through established SLAs is increasing women and adolescent girls beneficiaries’ participation in overall decision-making.   

All these results have been achieved through strategic partnerships with the Liberian Women Empowerment Network (LIWEN), White Rose Alliance (WRA), the Liberia Marketing Association (LMA), Liberia National Rural Women Structure (LNRWS), the Association of Women in Cross Border Trade, Action for Gender Equality (AGE), and the National Peace Hut Women of Liberia (NPOWOL).

14,500 stitch masks were produced by 18 women-led tailoring businesses to prevent COVID-19 infection. The masks were distributed to 1,958 community members (females: 1,614; males: 344) and 1,412 market women during awareness-raising activities. Beneficiaries are wearing masks and practicing social distancing. They are also engaged in handwashing to prevent infection. 

Over 575 women beneficiaries received funding to resuscitate their respective SLAs impacted by the pandemic. The SLAs are functioning as self-sustaining and self-managed groups. They are actively saving together, and members are taking loans out from their savings. Monitoring missions have found that food poverty amongst SLA members fell from 75% to 20% after just one year of saving. 

Some significant results in response to the socio-economic impact have been recorded:

1.	Peace, solidarity, and equality
•	Being part of such a successful community group has led to impressive gains in women’s social status during the crisis. Members are starting their businesses and taking part in household and community decision-making processes.
 
•	SLA members affected by the pandemic have stressed how their respective groups have helped to improve relations between them and surrounding communities. Peace has remained fragile in cross-border areas where these SLAs are contributing to the provision of a neutral platform for people to dialogue. 

2.	Making money work
•	The SLAs are not only helping women and their families to save their money during the pandemic or to access money. They are also helping them earn for increased economic security and better livelihood during and after the pandemic. 

UN Women continues to bring gender equality and human rights perspectives to its programming on HIV/AIDS with vulnerable women and adolescent girls. It works to ensure that no one is left behind and continues to implement and lead strategic interventions that make clear links to factors that are known to propel the epidemic, such as VAWG, denial of legal rights, and women’s inadequate participation in decision-making processes.
 
UN Women’s HIV/AIDS work has helped to increase the voices of women living with HIV, using tactics that promote their leadership and meaningful participation in all decisions and actions to respond to the epidemic. 
 
UN Women has contributed to the following SDGs:
-	SDG 1: End Poverty by investing in economic empowerment interventions (e.g., business development and access to finance for investing in small businesses, etc.) for reducing poverty and HIV vulnerability. This also includes help in keeping PLHIV healthy.
-	SDG 4: Ensure Quality Education by investing in access to adult education through the provision of literacy and numeracy skills classes for women and adolescent girls including the incorporation of HIV/AIDS training modules into UN Women’s literacy and business skills training curriculums. 
-	SDG 5: Achieve Gender Equality by investing in awareness-raising amongst religious, traditional, and community leaders including community members (men, women, boys, and girls), youth groups, and male networks (HeForShe) for social behavior change to address VAW, SGBV, and the acceptance of marginalized groups (e.g., LGBTQIA, PLHIV, and persons living with disability) to transform social norms, attitudes, and behaviors.

UNESCO plans to support the government of Liberia through the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Labour for strengthening their data and information management system offering capacity building training to the relevant officials as well as developing webpage in the Ministry's website. It is important that the database of these three ministries are comparatively analyzed and reports are produced to ensure access to need-based education and skills for all age-group learners including children, youth and adults. 

To address the gaps in data, UNICEF has provided critical support to the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection (MOGCSP) in launching the CPIMS+, to enhance the case management of vulnerable children. Currently operational in Montserrado County, the system is already facilitating the management of 204 cases (88 girls and 88 boys), demonstrating its immediate value in addressing the needs of vulnerable children. The implementation of the CPIMS+ system has strengthened the capacity of 43 social workers by providing a standardized and technology-driven approach to case management. To support CPIMS+, UNICEF procured and donated to the MOGCSP 60 tablets, 11 laptops, 5 laptops and 10 printers. UNICEF has also provided internet subscription. UNICEF has also supported the training of the 43 social workers and supervisors on the use of the system

planEntities.description:
In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of $57,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.2) to support several key initiatives in Liberia aimed at advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. These activities align with Activity ID: 2.1.2: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders.

The specific areas of support include:

1.) Development of a new gender and climate change action plan (ccGAP) to coincide with Liberia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0: Two consultancies are funded for this purpose, with $15,000 USD provided by UN Women Regional Office and $5,000 USD by UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution).

2.) Technical support for NDC 3.0 preparation and validation events: $10,000 USD is allocated by UN Women Regional Office for these crucial activities.

3.) Desk review consultancy to inform a project on Women in Cross-Border Trade (WICBT): $7,000 USD from UN Women Regional Office will support a review of the AfCFTA regional project proposal and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's strategic plan.

4.) Assessment of women's unpaid care work: $5,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will enable a thorough assessment conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection to understand the scope and impact of unpaid care responsibilities on women's lives.

5.) Documentation of experiences of vulnerable young women and women living with HIV/AIDS: $15,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will support the documentation of their perspectives on UN Women's economic empowerment efforts.

This comprehensive support from UN Women aims to contribute significantly to gender-responsive policy advocacy and decision-making across various sectors in Liberia.

WFP: 
WFP is providing technical and financial support for the comprehensive food security and nutrition assessment. WFP has contributed $30,000 USD apart from the $114,000 from USAID contribution.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: By 2024, targeted national institutions have the capacity to develop evidence-based cross-sectoral gender-responsive policy framework and accountability mechanisms that promote sustainable livelihoods, food security and resilience to climate change
planEntities.description:
13 women-based farming cooperatives are practicing climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture techniques. This is evidenced by the CSA techniques the women farmers are using in planting and growing rice, cassava, plantains, and maize (corn). The women are also practicing nutrition-sensitive agriculture demonstrated by their growing of different varieties of vegetables.  

WFP - 750 smallholder farmers received different training to enhance sustainable agriculture production and input support which helped them to adopt climate smart agriculture practices to increase production. Vulnerable farmer organizations resilience capacity strengthened through providing them with training, agricultural inputs, and machinery support to increase production and value addition.
Additionally, WFP created market access to smallholders farmer groups through purchase of locally grown food commodities (861.91 MT) at the value of US$1,900,000.00. This helped to boost agriculture production of smallholder farmers including increasing household incomes and improve food access for smallholder famers and families .

In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of 82,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.3) to support communities in Liberia to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, and food and nutrition security. This support aligns with "Activity ID: 2.1.3: Support communities to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, food and nutrition security, including the provision of agri-equipment, pre & post-harvest management training, etc" and encompasses several key initiatives.

Firstly, efforts to strengthen agricultural productivity and sustainability include Solar Power Agri-Equipment Support for Women Cooperatives, receiving two grants totaling 19,000 USD (14,000 USD from the UN Women HQ small grant and 5,000 USD from UN Women). This aims to enhance agricultural practices through the adoption of sustainable energy solutions. Secondly, promoting financial inclusion is addressed through Financial Inclusion Support for Women Cooperatives, allocated a budget of 20,000 USD from UN Women to improve women's access to formal financial services. A significant component focuses on Empowering Rural and Young Women through Capacity Building, with a budget of 25,000 USD from UN Women. This initiative targets women from UN Women-supported networks (e.g., NRWS, NaPHWoL, AWICBT, LMA, etc.) and will provide training in financial inclusion, green and blue economies, entrepreneurship and trade, care economy awareness and formalization, and digital literacy skills.

Furthermore, leveraging digital platforms and centers is a key strategy, with Scaling Up the Buy from Women Digital Platform and Establishing Digital Centers supported by a 10,000 USD budget from UN Women. This will enhance the digital platform and expand access to digital literacy and support centers. Building climate resilience and leadership is addressed through NDC 3.0 Training for Youth and Gender Climate Working Group, allocated 5,000 USD from UN Women for capacity building in climate action. Finally, Capacity Development on Organizational Development and Leadership Skills with AWICBT will receive 3,000 USD from UN Women to strengthen the organization.

These interconnected initiatives demonstrate UN Women's commitment in 2025 to fostering holistic and sustainable development for women in Liberia, aligning with the broader goals of increased productivity, enhanced livelihoods, and greater resilience.

WFP:
WFP is supporting 2,900 SHFs from 65 farmer groups in Grand Cape, Grand Bassa, Grand Gedeh, Bong, Nimba, Lofa, and Gbarpolu Counties. These farmers are receiving climate smart agriculture training, farmer tool and equipment (Power tillers, rice mills, cassava processors etc.), including storage and agri business facilities. WFP Liberia has linked these SHFs to its Home-Grown School Feeding Programme thus creating market access. The 2,900 SHFs received food assistance through value voucher redemption process from retailers. 300 hectares of lowland rice and vegetables are under cultivation.

planEntities.description:
Over 40 Savings and Loans Associations are:
Breaking down barriers to finance – The associations are helping the women overcome common barriers, and access to finance has been one such barrier for many of them because there is a lack of limited or no formal financial institutions in their communities.
Empowering women to become changemakers – The women in the associations are investing in CSA and vegetable production because of loans taken from their respective SLAs. They have been able to make a profit. Also, the SLAs are not just about increasing income or serving as a social protection fund, they have also empowered the women to become active players in their various communities.
Promoting solidarity and equality – Being part of such successful community associations has led to inspiring gains in the women’s social status. They are starting their own businesses and are participating in community decision-making processes at the household and community levels. Being able to contribute financially within their families has even put the women on a more equal footing with their spouses.
Contributing to peace building – financial freedom for women from a combination of the SLAs and other businesses is enabling women to support peacebuilding efforts at the community level. 

WFP:
WFP is providing 65 smallholder farmer groups access to micro finance through the VSLA activities under the Integrated Food Security and PBF-Projects. 

UNDP Accelerated Community Development Programme (ACDP) support rural women smallholder farmers with access to finance around food value chains.

planEntities.description:
UNDP Liberia: 
In 2024, the Programme continued to support government and civil society organizations (CSOs) to prevent and respond to GBV and pre-trial detention in Liberia. In this regard, the Programme continued its partnership with Development Education Leadership Training in Action Human Right Foundation (DELTA-HRF) and the Efficient Research and Development Institute (ERDI) that enhanced their capacity to support and mentor women led CSOs in Bong and Nimba counties to monitor the performance of Courts E and support GBV/SGBV survivors to access justice and needed services in their communities through the referral pathways. The women led CSOs, with support from DELTA-HRF and ERDI, also monitored the criminal justice system (police, courts, and prison) to identify bottlenecks in the processing of cases and to ensure that cases were processed accordingly. They further provided psychosocial support to survivors, supported survivors and witnesses to access the court (transportation), and conducted community awareness on the existence and functions of the Court E. 
The women led CSO networks in Bong and Nimba supported by DELTA-HRF and ERDI conducted community awareness and education activities on GBV and Court E through radio and community engagements/sensitization. Both DELTA-HRF and ERDI developed and aired radio jingles carrying messages on GBV and Court E on several radio stations in their respective counties. As shown in Table 2 below, the Programme, through these awareness and educational activities, reached 12,258 persons (4,390 men and 7,868 women) via community/house to house sensitization activities, as well as an estimated 80,515 persons through radio jingles. The awareness and education activities has increased the awareness and understanding of the communities on the working of Court E in these counties and enable them to provide support to survivors of GBV/SGBV and respect the rule of law.

planEntities.description:
In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of $57,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.2) to support several key initiatives in Liberia aimed at advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. These activities align with Activity ID: 2.1.2: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders.

The specific areas of support include:

1.) Development of a new gender and climate change action plan (ccGAP) to coincide with Liberia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0: Two consultancies are funded for this purpose, with $15,000 USD provided by UN Women Regional Office and $5,000 USD by UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution).

2.) Technical support for NDC 3.0 preparation and validation events: $10,000 USD is allocated by UN Women Regional Office for these crucial activities.

3.) Desk review consultancy to inform a project on Women in Cross-Border Trade (WICBT): $7,000 USD from UN Women Regional Office will support a review of the AfCFTA regional project proposal and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's strategic plan.

4.) Assessment of women's unpaid care work: $5,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will enable a thorough assessment conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection to understand the scope and impact of unpaid care responsibilities on women's lives.

5.) Documentation of experiences of vulnerable young women and women living with HIV/AIDS: $15,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will support the documentation of their perspectives on UN Women's economic empowerment efforts.

This comprehensive support from UN Women aims to contribute significantly to gender-responsive policy advocacy and decision-making across various sectors in Liberia.

WFP:

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: By 2024, targeted national institutions have the capacity to develop evidence-based cross-sectoral gender-responsive policy framework and accountability mechanisms that promote sustainable livelihoods, food security and resilience to climate change
planEntities.description:
13 women-based farming cooperatives are practicing climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture techniques. This is evidenced by the CSA techniques the women farmers are using in planting and growing rice, cassava, plantains, and maize (corn). The women are also practicing nutrition-sensitive agriculture demonstrated by their growing of different varieties of vegetables.  

WFP - 750 smallholder farmers received different training to enhance sustainable agriculture production and input support which helped them to adopt climate smart agriculture practices to increase production. Vulnerable farmer organizations resilience capacity strengthened through providing them with training, agricultural inputs, and machinery support to increase production and value addition.
Additionally, WFP created market access to smallholders farmer groups through purchase of locally grown food commodities (861.91 MT) at the value of US$1,900,000.00. This helped to boost agriculture production of smallholder farmers including increasing household incomes and improve food access for smallholder famers and families .

In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of 82,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.3) to support communities in Liberia to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, and food and nutrition security. This support aligns with "Activity ID: 2.1.3: Support communities to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, food and nutrition security, including the provision of agri-equipment, pre & post-harvest management training, etc" and encompasses several key initiatives.

Firstly, efforts to strengthen agricultural productivity and sustainability include Solar Power Agri-Equipment Support for Women Cooperatives, receiving two grants totaling 19,000 USD (14,000 USD from the UN Women HQ small grant and 5,000 USD from UN Women). This aims to enhance agricultural practices through the adoption of sustainable energy solutions. Secondly, promoting financial inclusion is addressed through Financial Inclusion Support for Women Cooperatives, allocated a budget of 20,000 USD from UN Women to improve women's access to formal financial services. A significant component focuses on Empowering Rural and Young Women through Capacity Building, with a budget of 25,000 USD from UN Women. This initiative targets women from UN Women-supported networks (e.g., NRWS, NaPHWoL, AWICBT, LMA, etc.) and will provide training in financial inclusion, green and blue economies, entrepreneurship and trade, care economy awareness and formalization, and digital literacy skills.

Furthermore, leveraging digital platforms and centers is a key strategy, with Scaling Up the Buy from Women Digital Platform and Establishing Digital Centers supported by a 10,000 USD budget from UN Women. This will enhance the digital platform and expand access to digital literacy and support centers. Building climate resilience and leadership is addressed through NDC 3.0 Training for Youth and Gender Climate Working Group, allocated 5,000 USD from UN Women for capacity building in climate action. Finally, Capacity Development on Organizational Development and Leadership Skills with AWICBT will receive 3,000 USD from UN Women to strengthen the organization.

These interconnected initiatives demonstrate UN Women's commitment in 2025 to fostering holistic and sustainable development for women in Liberia, aligning with the broader goals of increased productivity, enhanced livelihoods, and greater resilience.

WFP:
WFP is supporting 2,900 SHFs from 65 farmer groups in Grand Cape, Grand Bassa, Grand Gedeh, Bong, Nimba, Lofa, and Gbarpolu Counties. These farmers are receiving climate smart agriculture training, farmer tool and equipment (Power tillers, rice mills, cassava processors etc.), including storage and agri business facilities. WFP Liberia has linked these SHFs to its Home-Grown School Feeding Programme thus creating market access. The 2,900 SHFs received food assistance through value voucher redemption process from retailers. 300 hectares of lowland rice and vegetables are under cultivation.

planEntities.description:
UNDP Liberia: 
In 2024, the Programme continued to support government and civil society organizations (CSOs) to prevent and respond to GBV and pre-trial detention in Liberia. In this regard, the Programme continued its partnership with Development Education Leadership Training in Action Human Right Foundation (DELTA-HRF) and the Efficient Research and Development Institute (ERDI) that enhanced their capacity to support and mentor women led CSOs in Bong and Nimba counties to monitor the performance of Courts E and support GBV/SGBV survivors to access justice and needed services in their communities through the referral pathways. The women led CSOs, with support from DELTA-HRF and ERDI, also monitored the criminal justice system (police, courts, and prison) to identify bottlenecks in the processing of cases and to ensure that cases were processed accordingly. They further provided psychosocial support to survivors, supported survivors and witnesses to access the court (transportation), and conducted community awareness on the existence and functions of the Court E. 
The women led CSO networks in Bong and Nimba supported by DELTA-HRF and ERDI conducted community awareness and education activities on GBV and Court E through radio and community engagements/sensitization. Both DELTA-HRF and ERDI developed and aired radio jingles carrying messages on GBV and Court E on several radio stations in their respective counties. As shown in Table 2 below, the Programme, through these awareness and educational activities, reached 12,258 persons (4,390 men and 7,868 women) via community/house to house sensitization activities, as well as an estimated 80,515 persons through radio jingles. The awareness and education activities has increased the awareness and understanding of the communities on the working of Court E in these counties and enable them to provide support to survivors of GBV/SGBV and respect the rule of law.

planEntities.description:
In 2024, the Programme continued to provide support to the Judiciary to maintain and enhance the functionality of the Judicial Case Management Information System, which was established with the support of the Programme in 2021. The Programme provided advisory and technical support including upgrading of the functions and components of the digital case management system to be make more user-friendly. The Programme also paid the cost of hosting the digital system in the cloud and providing internet subscription that maintained the operations of the system during the year.
These supports helped to maintain the operations and functionality of the system, thereby leading to increased efficiency and effectiveness in tracking of cases on the dockets of magisterial courts across Montserrado County. The migration from manual case management to digital case management is a significant transformational change for the Judiciary, making the filing and retrieval of case files much easier and timely, which will subsequently contribute to reducing cases on courts dockets and reducing pre-trial detention in prisons. One of the reasons that had been attributed to docket and prison overcrowding is tracking cases through the system once the case has been indicted by the court.
The ease of collection, recording, organization, and retrieval of case information is significantly contributing to improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the Judiciary as the entity is able to access information and act on cases in real time, thus reducing the time it would normally take to dispense justice.  Lawyers and magistrates at magisterial courts in Montserrado County are now using the system to assist them plan and assign cases. This is expected to lead to reduction of cases on the courts’ dockets and by extension to the reduction of pretrial detainees in prisons. Pre-trial detention significantly contributes to prison overcrowding in Liberia, as more than 60% of the inmate population is pre-trial detainees.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.4: By 2024, public and private sector players have strengthened capacity to increase economic participation and productivity,  and in an inclusive manner enable employment, job creation and enterprise development.
planEntities.description:
In 2024, the Accelerated Community Development Programme (ACDP) delivered transformative impacts across rural Liberia by implementing key initiatives in water, agriculture, and health sectors. These efforts were designed to address critical gaps in basic services while empowering communities economically and socially.

The ACDP completed five solar-powered boreholes and 21 water kiosks in five rural communities across Gbarpolu, Bong, and Rivercess Counties. Four kiosks in Donfah, Bong County, are already operational, providing sustainable and clean drinking water. This initiative has significantly reduced the time and effort residents, particularly women and children, spend fetching water, improving overall quality of life.

The ACDP supported 14 farmers' cooperatives in six counties (Bomi, Bong, Gbarpolu, Lofa, Nimba, and Rivercess) with tractors, improved rice seeds, fertilizers, technical training, and financial assistance. These cooperatives cultivated large-scale rice and cassava crops, some for the first time. By December 2024, 12 cooperatives had harvested a total of 4,742 bags (25kg each) of paddy rice, benefiting 725 cooperative members (435 women, 290 men). These interventions are boosting productivity and transforming the livelihoods of cooperative members through sustainable income generation.

To enhance technical backstopping for rural farmers, the ACDP procured and handed over 16 YAMAHA motorbikes to the Ministry of Agriculture. These motorbikes were distributed to extension officers, enabling them to provide timely supervision, training, and monitoring. This logistical support has resolved longstanding challenges in reaching remote farming communities, ensuring consistent support to farmers.

The ACDP handed over seven ambulances to the Ministry of Health for deployment in rural health facilities across seven counties (Bomi, Lofa, Margibi, Maryland, Nimba, Rivercess, and River Gee). Since their deployment in July 2024, these ambulances have played a vital role in strengthening emergency medical responses, facilitating 340 emergency cases, including safe maternal deliveries. The ambulances have reduced referral times and improved access to critical healthcare services, significantly benefiting underserved rural communities.

planEntities.description:
In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of $57,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.2) to support several key initiatives in Liberia aimed at advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. These activities align with Activity ID: 2.1.2: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders.

The specific areas of support include:

1.) Development of a new gender and climate change action plan (ccGAP) to coincide with Liberia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0: Two consultancies are funded for this purpose, with $15,000 USD provided by UN Women Regional Office and $5,000 USD by UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution).

2.) Technical support for NDC 3.0 preparation and validation events: $10,000 USD is allocated by UN Women Regional Office for these crucial activities.

3.) Desk review consultancy to inform a project on Women in Cross-Border Trade (WICBT): $7,000 USD from UN Women Regional Office will support a review of the AfCFTA regional project proposal and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's strategic plan.

4.) Assessment of women's unpaid care work: $5,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will enable a thorough assessment conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection to understand the scope and impact of unpaid care responsibilities on women's lives.

5.) Documentation of experiences of vulnerable young women and women living with HIV/AIDS: $15,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will support the documentation of their perspectives on UN Women's economic empowerment efforts.

This comprehensive support from UN Women aims to contribute significantly to gender-responsive policy advocacy and decision-making across various sectors in Liberia.

planEntities.name: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: By 2024, targeted national institutions have the capacity to develop evidence-based cross-sectoral gender-responsive policy framework and accountability mechanisms that promote sustainable livelihoods, food security and resilience to climate change
planEntities.description:
In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of $57,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.2) to support several key initiatives in Liberia aimed at advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. These activities align with Activity ID: 2.1.2: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders.

The specific areas of support include:

1.) Development of a new gender and climate change action plan (ccGAP) to coincide with Liberia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0: Two consultancies are funded for this purpose, with $15,000 USD provided by UN Women Regional Office and $5,000 USD by UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution).

2.) Technical support for NDC 3.0 preparation and validation events: $10,000 USD is allocated by UN Women Regional Office for these crucial activities.

3.) Desk review consultancy to inform a project on Women in Cross-Border Trade (WICBT): $7,000 USD from UN Women Regional Office will support a review of the AfCFTA regional project proposal and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's strategic plan.

4.) Assessment of women's unpaid care work: $5,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will enable a thorough assessment conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection to understand the scope and impact of unpaid care responsibilities on women's lives.

5.) Documentation of experiences of vulnerable young women and women living with HIV/AIDS: $15,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will support the documentation of their perspectives on UN Women's economic empowerment efforts.

This comprehensive support from UN Women aims to contribute significantly to gender-responsive policy advocacy and decision-making across various sectors in Liberia.

planEntities.name: Support communities to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, food and nutrition security
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: By 2024, targeted national institutions have the capacity to develop evidence-based cross-sectoral gender-responsive policy framework and accountability mechanisms that promote sustainable livelihoods, food security and resilience to climate change
planEntities.description:
13 women-based farming cooperatives are practicing climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture techniques. This is evidenced by the CSA techniques the women farmers are using in planting and growing rice, cassava, plantains, and maize (corn). The women are also practicing nutrition-sensitive agriculture demonstrated by their growing of different varieties of vegetables.  

WFP - 750 smallholder farmers received different training to enhance sustainable agriculture production and input support which helped them to adopt climate smart agriculture practices to increase production. Vulnerable farmer organizations resilience capacity strengthened through providing them with training, agricultural inputs, and machinery support to increase production and value addition.
Additionally, WFP created market access to smallholders farmer groups through purchase of locally grown food commodities (861.91 MT) at the value of US$1,900,000.00. This helped to boost agriculture production of smallholder farmers including increasing household incomes and improve food access for smallholder famers and families .

In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of 82,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.3) to support communities in Liberia to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, and food and nutrition security. This support aligns with "Activity ID: 2.1.3: Support communities to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, food and nutrition security, including the provision of agri-equipment, pre & post-harvest management training, etc" and encompasses several key initiatives.

Firstly, efforts to strengthen agricultural productivity and sustainability include Solar Power Agri-Equipment Support for Women Cooperatives, receiving two grants totaling 19,000 USD (14,000 USD from the UN Women HQ small grant and 5,000 USD from UN Women). This aims to enhance agricultural practices through the adoption of sustainable energy solutions. Secondly, promoting financial inclusion is addressed through Financial Inclusion Support for Women Cooperatives, allocated a budget of 20,000 USD from UN Women to improve women's access to formal financial services. A significant component focuses on Empowering Rural and Young Women through Capacity Building, with a budget of 25,000 USD from UN Women. This initiative targets women from UN Women-supported networks (e.g., NRWS, NaPHWoL, AWICBT, LMA, etc.) and will provide training in financial inclusion, green and blue economies, entrepreneurship and trade, care economy awareness and formalization, and digital literacy skills.

Furthermore, leveraging digital platforms and centers is a key strategy, with Scaling Up the Buy from Women Digital Platform and Establishing Digital Centers supported by a 10,000 USD budget from UN Women. This will enhance the digital platform and expand access to digital literacy and support centers. Building climate resilience and leadership is addressed through NDC 3.0 Training for Youth and Gender Climate Working Group, allocated 5,000 USD from UN Women for capacity building in climate action. Finally, Capacity Development on Organizational Development and Leadership Skills with AWICBT will receive 3,000 USD from UN Women to strengthen the organization.

These interconnected initiatives demonstrate UN Women's commitment in 2025 to fostering holistic and sustainable development for women in Liberia, aligning with the broader goals of increased productivity, enhanced livelihoods, and greater resilience.

WFP:
WFP is supporting 2,900 SHFs from 65 farmer groups in Grand Cape, Grand Bassa, Grand Gedeh, Bong, Nimba, Lofa, and Gbarpolu Counties. These farmers are receiving climate smart agriculture training, farmer tool and equipment (Power tillers, rice mills, cassava processors etc.), including storage and agri business facilities. WFP Liberia has linked these SHFs to its Home-Grown School Feeding Programme thus creating market access. The 2,900 SHFs received food assistance through value voucher redemption process from retailers. 300 hectares of lowland rice and vegetables are under cultivation.

planEntities.description:
UNESCO plans to support the government of Liberia through the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Labour for strengthening their data and information management system offering capacity building training to the relevant officials as well as developing webpage in the Ministry's website. It is important that the database of these three ministries are comparatively analyzed and reports are produced to ensure access to need-based education and skills for all age-group learners including children, youth and adults. 

To address the gaps in data, UNICEF has provided critical support to the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection (MOGCSP) in launching the CPIMS+, to enhance the case management of vulnerable children. Currently operational in Montserrado County, the system is already facilitating the management of 204 cases (88 girls and 88 boys), demonstrating its immediate value in addressing the needs of vulnerable children. The implementation of the CPIMS+ system has strengthened the capacity of 43 social workers by providing a standardized and technology-driven approach to case management. To support CPIMS+, UNICEF procured and donated to the MOGCSP 60 tablets, 11 laptops, 5 laptops and 10 printers. UNICEF has also provided internet subscription. UNICEF has also supported the training of the 43 social workers and supervisors on the use of the system

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: By 2024, targeted national institutions have the capacity to develop evidence-based cross-sectoral gender-responsive policy framework and accountability mechanisms that promote sustainable livelihoods, food security and resilience to climate change
planEntities.description:
13 women-based farming cooperatives are practicing climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture techniques. This is evidenced by the CSA techniques the women farmers are using in planting and growing rice, cassava, plantains, and maize (corn). The women are also practicing nutrition-sensitive agriculture demonstrated by their growing of different varieties of vegetables.  

WFP - 750 smallholder farmers received different training to enhance sustainable agriculture production and input support which helped them to adopt climate smart agriculture practices to increase production. Vulnerable farmer organizations resilience capacity strengthened through providing them with training, agricultural inputs, and machinery support to increase production and value addition.
Additionally, WFP created market access to smallholders farmer groups through purchase of locally grown food commodities (861.91 MT) at the value of US$1,900,000.00. This helped to boost agriculture production of smallholder farmers including increasing household incomes and improve food access for smallholder famers and families .

In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of 82,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.3) to support communities in Liberia to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, and food and nutrition security. This support aligns with "Activity ID: 2.1.3: Support communities to increase productivity, enhance sustainable livelihoods, resilience capacities, social inclusion, financial inclusion, food and nutrition security, including the provision of agri-equipment, pre & post-harvest management training, etc" and encompasses several key initiatives.

Firstly, efforts to strengthen agricultural productivity and sustainability include Solar Power Agri-Equipment Support for Women Cooperatives, receiving two grants totaling 19,000 USD (14,000 USD from the UN Women HQ small grant and 5,000 USD from UN Women). This aims to enhance agricultural practices through the adoption of sustainable energy solutions. Secondly, promoting financial inclusion is addressed through Financial Inclusion Support for Women Cooperatives, allocated a budget of 20,000 USD from UN Women to improve women's access to formal financial services. A significant component focuses on Empowering Rural and Young Women through Capacity Building, with a budget of 25,000 USD from UN Women. This initiative targets women from UN Women-supported networks (e.g., NRWS, NaPHWoL, AWICBT, LMA, etc.) and will provide training in financial inclusion, green and blue economies, entrepreneurship and trade, care economy awareness and formalization, and digital literacy skills.

Furthermore, leveraging digital platforms and centers is a key strategy, with Scaling Up the Buy from Women Digital Platform and Establishing Digital Centers supported by a 10,000 USD budget from UN Women. This will enhance the digital platform and expand access to digital literacy and support centers. Building climate resilience and leadership is addressed through NDC 3.0 Training for Youth and Gender Climate Working Group, allocated 5,000 USD from UN Women for capacity building in climate action. Finally, Capacity Development on Organizational Development and Leadership Skills with AWICBT will receive 3,000 USD from UN Women to strengthen the organization.

These interconnected initiatives demonstrate UN Women's commitment in 2025 to fostering holistic and sustainable development for women in Liberia, aligning with the broader goals of increased productivity, enhanced livelihoods, and greater resilience.

WFP:
WFP is supporting 2,900 SHFs from 65 farmer groups in Grand Cape, Grand Bassa, Grand Gedeh, Bong, Nimba, Lofa, and Gbarpolu Counties. WFP Liberia has linked these SHFs to its Home-Grown School Feeding Programme thus creating market access. The 2,900 SHFs received food assistance through value voucher redemption process from retailers. 300 hectares of lowland rice and vegetables are under cultivation.

WFP:
WFP is implementing the Home-Grown School Feeding Programme and providing daily school meals to 77,264 school children from 324 public schools in Montserrado, Margibi, Bong, Nimba, and Maryland Counties. 
WFP had contracted 15 Farmer Cooperatives to aggregate and supply the 324 schools with locally grown rice, beans, red palm oil, and gari.

Currently operational in Montserrado County, the system is already facilitating the management of 204 cases (88 girls and 88 boys), demonstrating its immediate value in addressing the needs of vulnerable children. The implementation of the CPIMS+ system has strengthened the capacity of 43 social workers by providing a standardized and technology-driven approach to case management. To support CPIMS+, UNICEF procured and donated to the MOGCSP 60 tablets, 11 laptops, 5 laptops and 10 printers. UNICEF has also provided internet subscription. UNICEF has also supported the training of the 43 social workers and supervisors on the use of the system

planEntities.description:
In 2025, UN Women is providing a total of $57,000 USD (Activity ID: 2.1.2) to support several key initiatives in Liberia aimed at advancing gender equality and women's empowerment. These activities align with Activity ID: 2.1.2: Conduct gender responsive gap analyses, assessments, surveys, PHC, research studies at national and sub-national levels for informed policy advocacy and decision-making on WASH, Climate resilience, Food and nutrition security, political, social and economic empowerment of communities and stakeholders.

The specific areas of support include:

1.) Development of a new gender and climate change action plan (ccGAP) to coincide with Liberia's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0: Two consultancies are funded for this purpose, with $15,000 USD provided by UN Women Regional Office and $5,000 USD by UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution).

2.) Technical support for NDC 3.0 preparation and validation events: $10,000 USD is allocated by UN Women Regional Office for these crucial activities.

3.) Desk review consultancy to inform a project on Women in Cross-Border Trade (WICBT): $7,000 USD from UN Women Regional Office will support a review of the AfCFTA regional project proposal and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's strategic plan.

4.) Assessment of women's unpaid care work: $5,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will enable a thorough assessment conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection to understand the scope and impact of unpaid care responsibilities on women's lives.

5.) Documentation of experiences of vulnerable young women and women living with HIV/AIDS: $15,000 USD from UN Women Liberia (Sweden's contribution) will support the documentation of their perspectives on UN Women's economic empowerment efforts.

This comprehensive support from UN Women aims to contribute significantly to gender-responsive policy advocacy and decision-making across various sectors in Liberia.

WFP:

A significant component focuses on Empowering Rural and Young Women through Capacity Building, with a budget of 25,000 USD from UN Women. This initiative targets women from UN Women-supported networks (e.g., NRWS, NaPHWoL, AWICBT, LMA, etc.) and will provide training in financial inclusion, green and blue economies, entrepreneurship and trade, care economy awareness and formalization, and digital literacy skills.

Furthermore, leveraging digital platforms and centers is a key strategy, with Scaling Up the Buy from Women Digital Platform and Establishing Digital Centers supported by a 10,000 USD budget from UN Women. This will enhance the digital platform and expand access to digital literacy and support centers. Building climate resilience and leadership is addressed through NDC 3.0 Training for Youth and Gender Climate Working Group, allocated 5,000 USD from UN Women for capacity building in climate action. Finally, Capacity Development on Organizational Development and Leadership Skills with AWICBT will receive 3,000 USD from UN Women to strengthen the organization.

These interconnected initiatives demonstrate UN Women's commitment in 2025 to fostering holistic and sustainable development for women in Liberia, aligning with the broader goals of increased productivity, enhanced livelihoods, and greater resilience.

planEntities.description:
Over 40 Savings and Loans Associations are:
Breaking down barriers to finance – The associations are helping the women overcome common barriers, and access to finance has been one such barrier for many of them because there is a lack of limited or no formal financial institutions in their communities.
Empowering women to become changemakers – The women in the associations are investing in CSA and vegetable production because of loans taken from their respective SLAs. They have been able to make a profit. Also, the SLAs are not just about increasing income or serving as a social protection fund, they have also empowered the women to become active players in their various communities.
Promoting solidarity and equality – Being part of such successful community associations has led to inspiring gains in the women’s social status. They are starting their own businesses and are participating in community decision-making processes at the household and community levels. Being able to contribute financially within their families has even put the women on a more equal footing with their spouses.
Contributing to peace building – financial freedom for women from a combination of the SLAs and other businesses is enabling women to support peacebuilding efforts at the community level.

planEntities.description: Establish a Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) for Enhanced Protection Services to Migrants and Access to Safe Migration - The project establishes a Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) as a safe, neutral, one-stop support hub where migrants, regardless of status, can access gender-sensitive information, referral services, legal aid, health care, translation, and protection. It also conducts a needs assessment, raises awareness in migrant and host communities, and integrates systems to collect gender-disaggregated migration data. Through evidence generated by the MRC, the Government and stakeholders will better understand migrant protection needs, inform policies, and enhance responsiveness of services.

Through stakeholder consultations, technical support, and alignment with international standards, the project ensures that migrant health is protected and promoted as part of universal health coverage and national development priorities.

planEntities.description:
Strengthening Government Capacity to Develop an Integrated Approach to Migration Governance
- This project strengthens the capacity of the Government of Maldives to plan and implement an integrated, evidence-based, and gender-sensitive migration governance framework. It supports inter-agency coordination through the establishment of technical committees, development of a comprehensive Migration Policy and Integrated Border Management Strategy, and the creation of data systems to enable rights-based and coherent migration planning. By fostering institutional collaboration, policy alignment, and operational procedures, the project promotes inclusive, transparent, and accountable governance aligned with international standards and development objectives.

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: State institutions have enhanced capacity and demonstrate commitment to ensure access to non-discriminatory justice, rule of law and transitional justice for all.
planEntities.description: Combating Trafficking in Persons in Maldives - This component of the project focuses on strengthening the rule of law and institutional capacity to address trafficking in persons in the Maldives. It supports the enhancement of the national anti-trafficking legal framework, development and review of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), capacity building for law enforcement and justice sector actors, and improved coordination through the National Anti-Human Trafficking Steering Committee (NAHTSC). Through technical assistance, training, and legal reform, the project aims to ensure more effective victim identification, investigation, and prosecution of trafficking cases, while upholding international human rights and protection standards.

planEntities.name: The Project for Strengthening Capacity of Border Control for Responding to Infectious Diseases in Southwest Asia
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1:  The Government has strengthened capacity to establish and implement policies and initiatives which promote a dynamic, diversified and sustainable economy that delivers prosperity and opportunities to all, particularly for women.
planEntities.description: The Project for Strengthening Capacity of Border Control for Responding to Infectious Diseases in Southwest Asia - In collaboration with IOM Sri Lanka, the Maldives will upgrade capacity at Velana International Airport and Gan International Airport to better prevent the spread of infectious disease at borders. This includes providing contactless, health‑compliant infrastructure, document verification tools, traveler screening systems, and medical waste management. The project will train immigration and health staff in Maldives, introduce document examiners (Verifier TD&B units), and strengthen PoE health facilities to align with International Health Regulations (IHR 2005).

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: The Government, public and private sector and other stakeholders have strengthened capacities to put in place and operationalise enabling conditions and initiatives that ensure equal and inclusive access to sustainable livelihoods and decent employment, with a particular focus on increased labour participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities and those living on outer islands.
planEntities.description:
Strengthened capacity of Maldives Bureau of Statistics to monitor informal sector employment activities
 - The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has formed an unprecedented economic crisis all around the world. The hardest hit country in South Asia is the Maldives, an island nation heavily reliant on tourism with reported -30% reduction in GDP growth. UNDP conducted a Rapid Livelihood Assessment (RLA) in 2020 and estimated the livelihood impact of the nation's formal sector but found out that the impact on the informal sector remained largely unknown due to data gaps. This new study looks at data from the informal sector and is one of the first studies to assess the livelihood impact of Covid-19, specifically on the Maldivian informal sector. The report is highly relevant to the upcoming new CPD of UNDP outcome area 1 on inclusive, sustainable and thriving livelihoods. This outcome proposes that UNDP will work with the government to design policies and strategies to increase labour force participation of marginalized groups, such as women and people with disability. This survey presents critical information and data on informal sector - an area of the economy largely represented by marginalized groups and will help UNDP and Government to come up with informed policy recommendations to improve the livelihoods of this sector as the Maldives gears towards recovering from the pandemic.

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description: El objetivo del Proyecto es consolidar iniciativas comerciales sostenibles, eliminando o reduciendo las barreras relativas a la módica valoración de los servicios y productos ofrecidos por los bosques y humedales; y generando incentivos para la conservación de los ecosistemas y su biodiversidad. Este objetivo promueve que los pobladores locales, principalmente las comunidades nativas, desarrollen iniciativas de manejo, vigilancia y protección sostenible de los bosques y humedales, que, a su vez, les generen rentabilidad.

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a aumentar la productividad, competitividad y formalización del aparato productivo nacional a través del fortalecimiento de cadenas productivas sostenibles, con base en una economía circular y generación de empleos verdes, con enfoque intergeneracional e intercultural y en condiciones de igualdad de género.
planEntities.description: La CONFIEP ha identificado la necesidad de reevaluar su posicionamiento en el debate de las políticas enfocadas al desarrollo, reclamando un rol clave en los grandes temas relativos al modelo de desarrollo y reducción de la pobreza en el país, como representante del sector privado. En este sentido, una agenda que se quiere reforzar es aquella que permita visibilizar y reflejar el compromiso del empresariado con los desafíos del Perú en materia de derechos humanos en un espectro amplio (derechos económicos, sociales, civiles y políticos). Asimismo, teniendo en cuenta el peso de la informalidad y su reducción en la resolución de algunos de estos debates sobre el logro de un país más justo y cohesionado, CONFIEP, quiere realizar una aportación propia a la discusión esencial sobre el refuerzo de las políticas de protección social, y en especial sobre su alcance en las poblaciones más desprotegidas por la informalidad, así como la mejora de la eficiencia y cobertura de los mecanismos actuales de protección social en las empresas y trabajadores formales.

planEntities.name: Brindar asistencia técnica y acompañamiento a las organizaciones de trabajadores para contribuir con los siguientes entregables: 1) Estrategia sindical diseñada y actualizada   orientada a nuevos grupos de trabajadores (que laboran a través de plataformas digitales y teletrabajo) con enfoque de género y mejora de los servicios de representación, defensa y tutela de sus derechos laborales y sociales, así como, de formación y desarrollo de liderazgos sectoriales y territoriales; lo mismo respecto al sector de la agricultura de exportación y las TRH.  2) Las organizaciones de trabajadores cuentan con mayor conocimiento para hacer uso de una arquitectura funcional de coordinación sindical construida para impulsar el diálogo social y elaboración de propuestas de política pública 3) Fortalecidos los conocimientos del movimiento sindical y acordadas acciones para una incidencia efectiva en la implementación de los ODS y el MCC y promover la aceleración de la Agenda 2030, en base al relevamiento del ODS 8. 4)

planEntities.description: El objetivo estratégico de esta iniciativa es potenciar las capacidades de las organizaciones sindicales para elevar sus niveles de representatividad y una defensa efectiva de los trabajadores principalmente aquellos insertos en el marco de la economía de plataforma, modalidad de teletrabajo, economía informal, sector rural, economía del cuidado, así como fortalecer sus capacidades para la elaboración de propuestas y adopción de posiciones para promover el trabajo decente y los  derechos fundamentales con énfasis en libertad sindical y negociación colectiva en los diversos espacios de diálogo social desde donde e diseñan, ejecutan y/o de seguimiento a políticas públicas para una recuperación de la pandemia centrada en las personas, inclusiva, sostenible y resiliente. Se priorizará el trabajo en conjunto con las centrales sindicales y todas las acciones serán diseñadas y ejecutadas con perspectiva de género y de juventud.

planEntities.name: Providing Venezuelan migrants and refugees with access to decent jobs in their host countries - Enhancing opportunities for Venezuelan migrants and refugees in Latin America
planEntities.parentName: La población migrante y desplazada en situación de vulnerabilidad desprotección, pobreza e inseguridad alimentaria en un contexto de crisis de movilidad humana acceden a mecanismos e instrumentos que mejoran su capacidad de respuesta a través de la generación y mejoramiento de sus medios de vida frente a las crisis, implementados por las instituciones, actores nacionales y subnacionales.
planEntities.description:
El objetivo del proyecto es mejorar y aumentar los niveles de integración socioeconómica de los migrantes y refugiados venezolanos en sus países de acogida a través de un enfoque de trabajo decente. Con ese objetivo, la intervención buscará cuatro resultados:
* Mejora de la capacidad de los Institutos de Formación Profesional (IFP) para atender a la población nacional y a los migrantes y refugiados.
* Fortalecimiento del vínculo entre los Servicios Públicos de Empleo (SPE) y el mercado de trabajo para ofrecer oportunidades de empleo decente a los migrantes y refugiados venezolanos.
* Mejora de las oportunidades laborales para las mujeres venezolanas migrantes y refugiadas.
* Fortalecimiento de los sistemas de información del mercado laboral y de datos sobre migración laboral.

planEntities.description: Esta iniciativa tiene por objetivo fortalecer las capacidades de los actores del sector público y privado para abordar los principales retos de la formalización. Los resultados esperados son: (i) conocimiento generado sobre los obstáculos, beneficios e incentivos para la formalización en Perú para equipar mejor a los actores en la transición a la economía formal, (ii) capacidades fortalecidas de los actores para la identificación y aplicación de soluciones innovadoras, inclusivas y sensibles al género que promuevan una recuperación económica orientada a la transición a la economía formal, y (iii) evidencia generada sobre los incentivos a la formalización a través del pilotaje de nuevos enfoques para el diseño de estrategias o la revisión de las existentes. El grupo objetivo son las micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MIPYMES) formales con trabajadores informales, las MIPYMES informales y trabajadores informales por cuenta propia.

planEntities.name: SEGUIMIENTO EN TIEMPO REAL DE LAS AMENAZAS DE VIOLENCIA DE GÉNERO PARA MUJERES Y NIÑAS VENEZOLANAS DESPLAZADAS
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a ampliar la cobertura y el acceso, oportuno y de calidad a los servicios esenciales que promueven la protección y la atención de la violencia basada en género y otras prácticas nocivas en entornos humanitarios y de desarrollo.
planEntities.description:
"Contribuir a mejorar las estrategias de protección para prevenir la violencia de género y satisfacer las necesidades de las mujeres migrantes y refugiadas de Venezuela que son sobrevivientes de la violencia de género.
Este proyecto busca:
1) Identificar los riesgos de género, así como cómo, dónde y por qué ocurren para informar mejor estrategias preventivas y de protección.
2) Determinar qué servicios son más necesarios para las mujeres y niñas venezolanas refugiadas y migrantes y dónde, a lo largo de la ruta de migración, esos servicios serían más útiles y de más fácil acceso."

planEntities.name: Socioeconomic (Re)integratin Toolkit SA
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso al trabajo decente, a la vivienda digna y espacios públicos adecuados, y a un sistema integral de protección social, incluyendo un piso de protección social, que garantice seguridad económica, cobertura de salud y acceso a un sistema nacional de cuidados a lo largo de todo el ciclo vital, con énfasis en las poblaciones y territorios en situación de especial protección, o en situación de vulnerabilidad y/o precariedad, atendiendo las brechas de género, generacionales y por nacionalidad.
planEntities.description:
"Para ayudar a los gobiernos de América del Sur a fortalecer la recuperación socioeconómica posterior a la pandemia, la OIM está desarrollando un “juego de herramientas” de integración socioeconómica para que los funcionarios gubernamentales estén mejor equipados para facilitar la (re)integración de los migrantes y retornados en las economías nacionales y empoderar así a los migrantes y retornados como actores para el desarrollo sostenible.
Esto se logrará a través de dos componentes principales:
1) realizando una evaluación de evidencia rápida sensible al género para construir una base de evidencia sobre la (re)integración socioeconómica en América del Sur para el desarrollo e implementación de herramientas y;
2) poniendo a prueba el conjunto de herramientas y redactando un plan de implementación nacional para la (re)integración socioeconómica en los países piloto."

"Fortalecemiento de capacidades y competencias a Fiscales del Subsistema de Derechos Humanos y Terrorismo del Ministerio Público y  personal del Instituto de Medicina Legal, mediante el Curso Taller “Fortalecimiento de Competencias sobre Estándares Internacionales para la Investigación Fiscal de Violaciones a Derechos Humanos”, con el objetivo de garantizar una justicia pronta, efectiva e imparcial y, procurar la rendición de cuentas a favor de las víctimas y sus familiares.
Fortalecimiento de capacidades al Ministerio Público respecto a la aplicación de los estándares internacionales en derechos humanos y la jurisprudencia nacional e internacional, a través de un compendio que enfatice conceptos básicos en base a las principales sentencias nacionales e internacionales sistematizadas sobre derechos humanos, en particular, derecho a la protesta, reunión pacífica, uso de la fuerza y violaciones a derechos humanos.  
Fortalecer capacidades y competencias de los/as fiscales del Ministerio Público y el personal del Instituto de Medicina Legal, en el marco del Protocolo de Berkeley, el cual contiene los primeros Estándares internacionales para la sistematización e investigación de redes sociales como evidencias en violaciones a derechos humanos.
Fortalecer las capacidades y competencias de los y las fiscales del Ministerio Público y de Medicina Legal en la utilidad, importancia y uso práctico de los protocolos de Estambul y de Minnesota y las técnicas forenses de investigación"

planEntities.name: Gestión de residuos orgánicos en Perú: acelerando el progreso hacia un sector de residuos circular y neutro en carbono
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description:
"El objetivo general de los Proyectos de Apoyo a la NAMA o Acción de Mitigación Nacionalmente Apropiada (NSP) es acelerar la implementación de proyectos de tratamiento de residuos orgánicos y de captura de gases de vertedero, contribuyendo a la NDC de Perú y proporcionando importantes co-beneficios de desarrollo sostenible en el contexto de la recuperación de Covid-19, como la reducción de la contaminación, la inclusión social y la creación de empleos verdes. La NDC de Perú considera prioritario el sector de los residuos, y este NSP apoyará directamente todas las medidas incluidas en él.

Se espera que el  NPS apoye directamente el desarrollo de una cartera de aproximadamente 22 proyectos. Entre ellos se encuentran un proyecto de captura de gas de vertedero que genera electricidad limpia, seis proyectos de digestión anaeróbica y 15 proyectos de compostaje. Además, el NPS creará una cartera de 40 proyectos con estudios de prefactibilidad para aumentar la replicabilidad del modelo del NPS y atraer más inversiones."

planEntities.name: Proyecto "De la migración a la integración: construyendo comunidades productivas y protectoras"
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso, la calidad y la permanencia en los servicios educativos para desarrollar los logros de aprendizaje y contribuir al bienestar integral de los y las estudiantes, de manera inclusiva, equitativa y en condiciones de igualdad de genero, de derechos, interculturalidad, asegurando una educación a lo largo de la vida para la población en general, y con énfasis en poblaciones vulnerables y en territorios priorizados.
planEntities.description:
"Facilitar la construcción de comunidades refugiadas y migrantes integradas y productivas mediante el acceso a medios de vida sostenibles, el acceso a la educación de calidad en el sistema público y el disfrute de derechos humanos. 
El objetivo del proyecto es que los migrantes, refugiados y otras personas desplazadas se conviertan en miembros productivos de la comunidad de acogida y trabajen juntos para promover la resiliencia común, el crecimiento socioeconómico y el fortalecimiento de la diversidad cultural. En este sentido, el proyecto buscará: 1) Incrementar el acceso a los derechos culturales y educativos como servicios básicos para las personas afectadas por el desplazamiento; y 2) generar oportunidades de ingresos y medios de subsistencia para las personas afectadas por el desplazamiento han aumentado a través de las industrias culturales y las artes."

La EDS proporciona a los estudiantes de todas las edades conocimientos, competencias, valores y el poder de acción necesarios para cuidar el planeta y abordar desafíos como el cambio climático, la pérdida de biodiversidad, la utilización no sostenible de los recursos y las desigualdades. Asimismo, mejora las dimensiones cognitivas, socioemocionales y comportamentales del aprendizaje.

planEntities.name: Proyecto de Reservas de Biosfera (RB) de la gran cuenca amazónica: RB Manu y RB Oxapampa-Asháninka-Yánesha
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description: Contribuir a la resiliencia de 2 Reservas de Biosfera (RB) de la Amazonía peruana creando un modelo sostenible de relaciones entre las comunidades y el medio ambiente, a través del apoyo a las iniciativas de conservación y económicas que se desarrollan en las RB y sus alrededores. El proyecto tiene un componente de coproducción de conocimiento en cuatro temas: 1) acción climática y reducción del riesgo de desastres; 2) acciones integradas de conservación y desarrollo en apoyo a actividades productivas en 9 distritos (cafe, aguaymanto, piscicultura y apicultura); 3) conservación de bosques y manejo de incendios; 4) restauración de sistemas hídricos y forestales.

planEntities.name: Proyecto Libertad de Expresión y Seguridad de Periodistas/ Acceso Universal a la Información y Alfabetización Mediática
