planEntities.description:
"1. Consolidar en el Perú una agenda para la prevención y promoción de la libertad de expresión, seguridad de periodistas y la lucha contra la impunidad en los delitos contra los mismos, a través de sinergias y diálogos entre los diferentes poderes del Estado, sociedad civil y asociaciones de periodistas, en el marco del Plan de las Naciones unidas sobre Seguridad de Periodistas y el plan de Acción de la Haya.
2. Sensibilizar y generar incidencia sobre el acceso universal a la información y a la alfabetización mediática."

planEntities.description:
"
Contribuir al desarrollo organizacional del Pacto por la Cultura al 2030, un mecanismo innovador que genera alianzas entre el sector privado, público y la cooperación internacional con el objetivo de apoyar iniciativas en 4 líneas estratégicas de acción: 1) Condiciones para el desarrollo de industrias culturales y creativas sostenibles, con un enfoque generador de capacidades y mercado. 2) Gestión integrada, sostenible y resiliente del patrimonio cultural con enfoque territorial. 3) Estrategias para prevenir el racismo y fortalecer la valoración y protección de la diversidad cultural. 4)Fortalecimiento de la gobernanza e institucionalidad cultural en el país."

planEntities.description: Una EER proporciona una evaluación equilibrada de lo que se sabe (y lo que no se sabe) en la literatura científica sobre una intervención, un problema o una cuestión práctica, utilizando una metodología sistemática para buscar y evaluar críticamente los estudios empíricos. Sin embargo, para ser "rápida", una EER hace concesiones en relación con la amplitud, la profundidad y la exhaustividad de la búsqueda. La importancia de incorporar a la EER un enfoque que tenga en cuenta el género se debe a que la integración, la edad y la diversidad (es decir, el origen social/étnico) son variables cruciales que influyen en la trayectoria de (re)integración de los distintos grupos.

planEntities.name: Apoyo al fortalecimiento de capacidades para la transición a la movilidad eléctrica (Proyecto MOVE LATAM)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.5 Implementadas políticas, acciones y medidas de prevención y reducción de la contaminación ambiental y de emisiones tanto en el ámbito urbano como rural.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto GCF readiness “Avanzando con un enfoque regional hacia la movilidad eléctrica en América Latina”  tiene el objetivo general de promover el avance en 14 países de la región de la descarbonización del sector transporte promoviendo la formación del ecosistema habilitante para la movilidad eléctrica. 

El proyecto tiene los siguientes objetivos especificos: 1) Se fortalece la capacidad regional para evaluar la tecnología de movilidad eléctrica en el contexto de estrategias más amplias de mitigación del cambio climático, 2) Se identifican y mejoran las políticas públicas y modelos de negocio habilitantes para ampliar la adopción de movilidad eléctrica, 3) Se fortalecen las estrategias de financiamiento climático y el pipeline nacional. 

En Paraguay las contrapartes del proyecto son la NDA- el Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible- y el Viceministerio de Transporte (MOPC- Ministerio Obras Públicas y Comunicaciones) en conjunto con la Secretaria Técnica de Planificación (STP).

planEntities.description:
La temporada  2020-2021 culminó en septiembre de 2021 con 17.052 hectáreas de siembra mecanizada de rubros de consumo y renta, incluyendo la habilitación de nuevas parcelas correspondientes a 1.674 hectáreas aptas para la mecanización en 43 distritos de los departamentos de San Pedro, Concepción, Canindeyú, Caazapá, Caaguazú, Alto Paraná, Horqueta, Cordillera y Guairá. 
12.846 personas fueron beneficiarios/as de DIAFPA en el 2020/2021, de las cuales el 44.2% son mujeres.
Las hectáreas trabajadas representan ingresos en comercialización por un total de 46.328.101.770 guaraníes (USD 6.914.642) en los rubros de sésamo, soja y maíz (grano seco y choclo).
28 MIPYMES rurales capacitadas en temas gerenciales, técnicos y administrativos; 50% de ellas lideradas por mujeres.
100% de las MIPYMES finalizaron el curso con planes comerciales específicos vinculados a cadenas de valor orientadas al mapeo e identificación de potenciales nichos de mercado, la diversificación de fuentes de ingresos y la construcción de redes empresariales de negocios.
Las 28 MIPYMES participantes decidieron firmar un acuerdo entre sí para la formación de una asociación nacional de segundo piso llamada Unión de productores y MIPYMES del Paraguay.
Luego de estas capacitaciones, se pudo ver un aumento en un 50% de participación de empresas locales en los llamados y/o procesos licitatorios de los proyectos.

planEntities.description:
8.000 kits de alimentos fueron distribuidos a familias de comunidades indígenas a través del Instituto Paraguayo del Indígena (INDI). 
Familias damnificadas en diferentes puntos del país fueron atendidas con la entrega de 38.500 kits de alimentos, 33.330 chapas de zinc y 3.330 colchones a través de la Secretaría de Emergencia Nacional (SEN).
Entrega de medicamentos y equipos biomédicos al Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social en Alto Paraná. Entre ellos, se destacan: 
38.000 unidades de Midazolam, 22.000 unidades de Besilato de Atracurio, 3.500 unidades de Noradrenalina, 2.000 unidades de Enoxaparina, 2.000 unidades de Ceftriaxona, 1.200 unidades de Levofloxacina, 1.200 unidades de Vancomicina  y 200 unidades de Colistina.  
12 ventiladores pulmonares, 8 camas eléctricas para terapias, 8 flujometros y 8 reguladores para oxígeno medicinal, 8 equipos generadores de alto flujo, 2 carros de paro, 1 electrocardiógrafo, 5.000 sets para bomba de infusión, 10 monitores multiparamétricos, 1 cardiodesfibrilador, 8 aspiradores portátiles de secreciones. 
Entrega de 14.840 unidades de placas petri a la Red Nacional de Laboratorios del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social, los cuales se utilizan para cultivar muestras en pruebas diagnósticas que beneficiarán a unas 15.000 personas aproximadamente.

planEntities.name: National capacities supported and strengthened to effectively prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons in accordance with international standards and best practices, and to achieve sustainable impact through implementation of the National Action Plan against TiP
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description:
UNODC has been engaged with the Saudi Human Rights Commission (HRC), as chair entity of the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking (NCCHT) since February 2020 in a multi-phased project of technical cooperation in the field of combating trafficking in persons (TiP). Therethrough, UNODC supports national efforts spearheaded by the HRC/NCCHT in preventing and combating TiP through a victim-centred approach that upholds the rights of trafficked and potential victims to protection, support, and care in line with international standards and norms and best practices.
Achievements under Phase I (February 2020 - August 2022) include the launch of the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) on 31 March 2020 which is currently managed by a central team in Riyadh together with 13 sub-teams in all regions across the Kingdom for effective coordination in dealing with TiP cases; the establishment of TiP specialized courts in all regions of the Kingdom with 124 prosecutors; the creation of the first-ever anti-TiP specialized Prosecution Unit on 30 July 2022; the creation of a specialized TiP Data Management Team; the development and adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat TiP (2021-2023); the legislative review and reform of the Kafala sponsorship system; and the delivery of 33 capacity-building activities that benefited over 1,600 officials within government entities, institutions, and CSOs.
Phase II (3 years, launched in March 2023) focuses on sustaining the outcomes of Phase I and further supporting the Kingdom through the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) against TiP. Activities include reviewing and updating the NRM; developing the electronic format of the NRM to support the availability, accuracy, and timeliness of TiP-related data; building monitoring and evaluation capacities for the implementation of the NAP; raising awareness of labour dispute committees, the media, the private sector and through religious authorities; conducting legislative and policy reviews; strengthening national capacities of law enforcement and criminal justice for the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of TiP cases; supporting the creation of a national training resource/hub on preventing and combating TiP; and promoting the creation of partnerships for knowledge and best practices exchange.

planEntities.description: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) is a collaborative initiative among five UN Agencies (UNEP, UNDP, UNIDO, UNITAR, and ILO) to support countries in transforming their economies towards green and inclusive models, aligned with the 2030 SDG Agenda and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. In Thailand, PAGE is led by UNIDO and the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC).Key Achievements:1) Greening National Policies and Strategies:Green Economy Policy Scoping Report: Highlights the reforms needed for decarbonization, promoting the Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) model, renewable energy, green finance, digitalization, and capacity development.Green and Inclusive Economic Recovery Policy Assessment Report: Recommends integrating SDGs, Nationally Determined Contributions, and BCG Economic Policy into government projects and budgeting. Developed training modules focused on green and inclusive development, measuring progress with green indicators, and principles of green industry and jobs.2) Carbon Cap and Trade for a Decarbonized Economy:Macroeconomic Planning for Green and Climate Policy Options Report and Training: Strengthens government capacity to make informed economic policy decisions, assessing socio-economic impacts of carbon tax, energy efficiency, renewable energy investments, and bio-circular-green economy investments.Emission Trading Scheme Development: Promotes national-level carbon market development, analyzing carbon pricing mechanisms and socio-economic impacts. Workshops and workplans were developed for implementing ETS in Thailand, covering all aspects from regulation to capacity building.3) Digitalization of Financing Mechanism for Sustainable Waste Management:Based on assessments and collaborations with the Department of Local Administration, mobile applications are being developed to enhance local government capacities in managing waste cycles sustainably.

planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description:
This suboutput comprises of multiple ILO projects:
1. TRIANGLE in ASEAN (2011 - 2025)
2. TRIANGLE Partnerships (2026 - 2031)
3. Realizing Women Migrant Workers' Rights and Opportunities in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations - Safe and Fair (2018 -2023)
4. Ensuring decent work and reducing vulnerabilities for women and children in the context of labour migration in Southeast Asia - PROTECT (2024 - 2027) 
5. SEA on Labour Migration in the Fishing Sector (S2SR SEA Phase II, 2020 - 2024)
6. Ship to Shore Rights in SEA: Safe Migration for Decent Work in the Blue Economy (S2SR SEA Phase III, 2025 - 2028)

Focus areas for the ILO's labour migration programming include protecting and promoting of the rights of women and men migrant workers including on fair recruitment and working conditions; contributing to economic development and inclusive growth – in particular labour mobility, skills development and recognition, and increasing development impact; contributing to climate resilience; reintegration; advocacy (with UNHCR) on labour market access for refugees and forcibly displaced persons; supporting national and regional dialogues on labour migration; and improving harmonised data collection and statistics.

Reported by: Dip Mager, OHCHR
Date: 9 April 2025, 23:09
The OHCHR Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRD) project/activity was suspended pending the review of Thailand by the CEDAW Committee. The project, funded by Sweden, was designed to support WHRD women survivors of human rights violations and their families’ engagement with the CEDAW review process. planEntities.name: State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women empowerment to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level to promote women peace and cybersecurity and digital literacy.
planEntities.parentName: Good governance, rule of law and social contract are enhanced for SDG acceleration
planEntities.description:
In 2023, following the advice of UN Women, the agency combined two sub-outputs and modified the sub-output statement accordingly. The original sub-output (SOU 7) aimed to enhance the knowledge and mechanisms of state and non-state actors to promote gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $60,000, but only $20,000 was available, and the expenditure was $56,426. To address this inconsistency, the available resource amount was adjusted to $56,426.

The second sub-output (SOU 11) focused on the Royal Thai Government (RTG) acquiring knowledge on gender-responsive approaches to prioritize gender equality and women's empowerment in budgeting and procurement at the local and national levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $10,000, with $5,000 available and $2,000 expended.

Now, these two sub-outputs have been integrated into a revised sub-output (Revised SOU 7). The revised statement emphasizes that state and non-state actors have increased their knowledge and mechanisms to advance gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. Additionally, it includes a specific focus on gender-responsive budgeting as a means to promote the prioritization of gender equality and women's empowerment.


The original sub-output statement (SOU 7): State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women's empowerment  and to integrate/mainstream gender-responsive approach in their policy or operational framework at national and local level
The original sub-output statement (SOU 11): The Royal Thai Government (RTG) gain the knowledge on gender-responsive approach to advance gender responsive budgeting/procurement at local and national level to ensure that gender equality and women's empowerment are prioritized.

The integrated sub-output is now (Revised SOU 7): "State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level including gender-responsive budgeting to promote prioritization of gender equality and women empowerment. "

planEntities.name: Country capacity strengthened for health emergency preparedness, prevention, detection and response through enhanced health security systems, emergency operations, risk communication, community engagement, mass gathering preparedness, and implementation of the International Health Regulations (IHR).
planEntities.parentName: Capacities for low carbon society, resilience, post-COVID 19 and disaster recovery with capability to adapt and reduce the risks of disasters are enabled and strengthened.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Improving national capability to prepare, prevent, detect and respond to public health emergencies (PHE)" (ID 82366); "Regional health security and national risk assessment capacities strengthened" (ID 207683); "Emergency response operations and mass gathering preparedness supported" (ID 207684); "National health security capacities and IHR systems strengthened" (ID 207685); and "Risk communication and community-based emergency preparedness strengthened" (ID 207686). WHO supported the establishment of the Secretariat for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED) and strengthened national surveillance by integrating the Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment (QIRA) tool into the Standard Operating Procedures of National Situation Awareness Teams. Emergency response capacity was bolstered through procurement of essential supplies for the cholera response to spillover cases from Myanmar, the provision of shelter and psychosocial support materials for the border conflict response, and support to the Ministry of Public Health for mass gathering preparedness during the SEA Games. National preparedness was further enhanced through implementation of the Hospital Safety Index across Ministry of Public Health hospitals, strengthened provincial Emergency Operations Center capacities, upgraded Event-Based and genomic Surveillance for respiratory pathogens in high-tourism locations, and establishment of the National IHR Authority. Risk communication was advanced by piloting the Information Environment Assessment to address infodemics and by strengthening linkages between the Public Health Emergency Operations Center's risk communication channels and Village and Migrant Health Volunteer networks.

planEntities.name: Digital health and innovation advanced to improve service delivery through interoperable health information systems, strengthened health data governance, and scalable digital solutions that address emerging health challenges.
planEntities.parentName: Digital transformation, digital inclusion, and innovation for human capital optimization are enabled.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "Advance digital health and innovation for equitable service delivery" (ID 182897) and "Digital Health Platforms and Health Information System (HIS) is strengthened" (ID 82410). The digital health ecosystem was strengthened through improved governance, legislation and compliance with Health Information Exchange standards and cybersecurity protocols, alongside support to the Global Initiative on Digital Health architecture and promotion of safe, equitable use of artificial intelligence. A national strategy to standardize health data collection across public and private facilities was introduced, complemented by an Open Data approach enabling real-time public health data sharing among researchers and policymakers, as well as development of interoperability standards, health data governance frameworks, and virtual hospital and telemedicine platforms.

planEntities.name: Health and well-being improved through a transformed workforce and integrated action on the social, behavioural and environmental determinants of health,  including evidence-based parenting, violence prevention, road safety, healthy ageing, healthy cities, digital mental health services and NCD risk reduction.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Facilitate and enhance integrated care for older people through the use of mobile health technology" (ID 82412); "Progressive development of legislation on control of marketing of food and non-alcoholic beverage for children" (ID 82467); "Health policies and collective action against NCDs... (Strategies 1 and 2)" (ID 82468); "Evidence-based parenting and violence prevention programs scaled up" (ID 207692); and "Urban governance for Healthy Cities strengthened" (ID 207695). Integrated care for older people was advanced through mobile health technology, complementing broader NCD policy work that promoted increased investment in NCDs through targeted communication strategies based on Thailand's scale-up findings, aligned with NCD Strategies 1 and 2. Legislative development on marketing controls for food and non-alcoholic beverages targeting children was progressed through technical support and policy advocacy, contributing to the wider NCD risk-reduction agenda. Child protection and development were fostered through the scale-up of evidence-based parenting programmes and high-level advocacy, complemented by the 2nd global survey on Violence Against Children to generate data for policy formulation. Urban health governance was strengthened through capacity building for local authorities, with the Healthy Cities approach recognized through awards to four Thai cities for their commitment to health-promoting urban environments.

planEntities.name: Disease burden reduced through strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship, accelerated neglected tropical disease elimination efforts, and implementation of evidence-informed policies and multisectoral actions for noncommunicable disease prevention and control.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates eight former sub-outputs: "Promoting evidence-based advocacy and implementing robust health and economic monitoring mechanisms for managing NCDs... (Strategies 3, 4 & 5)" (ID 82469); "Improve the quality and reach of essential health services" (ID 182895); "National workforce strategies strengthened and National Health Assembly resolution 2024 on transforming workforce for healthy society" (ID 207682); "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) surveillance and stewardship enhanced" (ID 207687); "Neglected Tropical Disease elimination and treatment supported" (ID 207690); "Mental health promotion, surveillance, and digital services expanded" (ID 207691); "Healthy ageing and integrated care for older people promoted" (ID 207696); and "NCD risk factor reduction policies and enforcement mechanisms strengthened" (ID 207697). Multisectoral action on NCDs was enhanced through improved partnerships facilitated by the UN Thematic Working Group, aligned with NCD Strategies 3, 4 and 5, complementing the workforce strengthening achieved through enhanced HRH provider registries and a landscape analysis of the community non-professional workforce. Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) management was advanced through co-hosting a Multi-Country Meeting on AMR and Primary Health Care, a Point Prevalence Survey on healthcare-associated infections across 100 hospitals, and development of a national AMR burden methodology and antimicrobial stewardship tools. Progress towards elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases was supported through provision of diagnostic test strips for Lymphatic Filariasis and sustained treatment of leprosy cases through procurement and distribution of essential medication. Mental health services were expanded through the nationwide scale-up of the "Step-by-Step" digital application, the "Tor term Jai" platform, and the WHO LIVE LIFE suicide prevention package, alongside capacity building through the 3rd International Mental Health Workforce Training. Healthy ageing was promoted through implementation of the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach with Siriraj Hospital, alongside advocacy to address social isolation among older persons. NCD risk factor reduction was advanced through sustained advocacy for "Best Buys" policies, including health taxes, e-cigarette bans, food reformulation, Milk Code enforcement, and alcohol control policy assessment.

planEntities.name: Migrant health equity advanced through strengthened migrant health management systems, improved health literacy, and multisectoral action to support inclusive and people-centred health services for migrants and non-national populations.
planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs that together form WHO's Migrant Health Initiative: "Strengthening migrant health management system" (ID 82490) and "Improving the health literacy among migrants and their communities" (ID 82497), which receive an equal proportion of funding. Access to health services for migrants was improved through advancement of the Migrant Health Strategy and expansion of the HINT data platform to include migrant populations, alongside strengthened health literacy among migrants and their communities, including workplaces, through policy advocacy, networking, social movement and policy research to advance health equity for migrants and non-national populations. Operational capacity was further strengthened through field visits, training and improved human resource management for migrant health.

planEntities.name: Thailand’s role in shaping key global health agendas and advancing sustainable health development strengthened through enhanced leadership, knowledge sharing, evidence-informed decision-making, and international collaboration, while supporting implementation of national health priorities and Country Cooperation Strategy outcomes.
planEntities.parentName: Good governance, rule of law and social contract are enhanced for SDG acceleration
planEntities.description: This sub-output is carried forward from the former sub-output: "Promoting the demonstrated collective leadership and contributions of Thailand in global health" (ID 90382), under the CCS EnLIGHT priority area of the 2022-2026 Country Cooperation Strategy. It enhances Team Thailand's collective capacity for international engagement in global health governance, focusing on two core functions: advancing key global health agendas and supporting other Country Cooperation Strategy programmes and partner agencies. This is achieved through four strategic actions: evidence generation, capacity development, international engagement, and knowledge management, including the establishment of resource centres and platforms and effective policy communication to support policy decisions.

planEntities.name: Road safety strengthened, with a particular focus on motorcycle users, through a national master plan, strengthened road safety cooperation mechanisms, laws and policy implementation, and enhanced capacity of stakeholders and actors to address road safety challenges.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "A national master plan for motorcycle safety developed" (ID 199373) and "Road safety enhanced with a particular focus on motorcycle users... (RSF)" (ID 210025). WHO supported the development of Thailand's first national Master Plan focused specifically on motorized two-wheeler safety, in response to the country's high rate of road traffic fatalities, of which nearly 80 per cent involve motorized two-wheelers, in partnership with the Department of Disease Control (DDC) and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation. This was complemented by road safety initiatives advanced through engagement with the Parliamentary Advisory Committee, implementation of the UN Road Safety Fund project, and improved hospital injury surveillance systems to inform road safety interventions.

planEntities.name: GEF-7 Project “Promoting the Transition to a Circular Economy in Uruguay” under UNIDO GCIP platform
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1. Sustainable production and consumption models developped and validated in strategic sectors of the economy, that include and test new technologies/practices following the principles of circular economy, strengthen the development of the bioeconomy and favour resilience and inclusion.
planEntities.description: The project focuses in two main sectors of the country: i) Agri-food Systems with the promotion of cleantech waste valorization technologies (including bio-fuels and bio-fertilizers, biochemical products recovery) & ii) Country Renewable Energy Matrix, by promoting methods and technologies that allow the storage and use electrical energy surplus. The initiative focuses on the development and transfer of state-of-the-art technologies, contributing to the development of a professional sector in the field of engineering and consultancy that will lead to the improvement of the technological basis of the country.

planEntities.name: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE)

planEntities.description: PAGE integrates technical capacities of five UN Agencies and supports countries wishing to embark on greener and more inclusive growth trajectories. Since 2018, Uruguay has become a partner country of the Programme and seven National Ministries (Office of Planning and Budget, Ministry of Industry, Ministry of Finance, National Agency for International Cooperation, Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Environment), work together to achieve national goals on green economy. Main technical areas of PAGE in Uruguay are: Planning for Green Economy, Circular Economy, Green Jobs, Green and Inclusive Production and Services, Capacity Building.

planEntities.parentName: Resilience [Enhanced capacity and gender-responsive policies to identify and reduce climate risks, respond to disasters and build the resilience of vulnerable populations]
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed project is to reduce vulnerability to climate change in the Greater Mekong Sub-region. This objective will be achieved through three complementary outcomes: 
(1)	Climate change adaptation interventions, particularly EbA, implemented by vulnerable communities in the GMS to manage climate change impacts, particularly droughts and floods;
(2)	Enhanced knowledge and awareness of adaptation measures, including EbA, to shared climate change impacts in different ecosystems to promote regional cooperation, planning and implementation of adaptation in the GMS; and 
(3)	Strengthened regional cooperation.

planEntities.name: Build technical capacities of value chain actors for efficient and inclusive sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chains in Tanzania (AFDP)
planEntities.parentName: Relevant institutions have improved capacities to provide gender-responsive, market-oriented, quality programmes, infrastructure/facilities, products, and services to MSMEs and small holder farmers
planEntities.description:
Support to strengthen sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chain in Tanzania. i) designed to enhance market access, value addition, and private sector development for smallholder farmers. Its core strategy revolves around improving the seed business and fish market systems, with a strong emphasis on sustainable agricultural practices and inclusive growth. The programme aims to increase the use of quality seeds by supporting a sustainable supply of locally adapted and climate-resilient varieties. This effort targets 25% of local farming activities, enabling farmers to replace open-pollinated varieties every three years while building their capacity to maintain seed quality. To achieve its goals, AFDP focuses on four strategic areas. First, it establishes regional multi-stakeholder innovation platforms that bring together public, private, and associative actors. These platforms coordinate seed demand and supply, promote climate-smart agriculture, and support the development of professional seed producer and distributor organizations. They also facilitate annual stakeholder meetings and use digital tools for planning and monitoring seed-related activities. Second, the programme strengthens the supply and accessibility of improved seeds by developing agro-dealer networks and village input shops, particularly those managed by women and youth. It promotes partnerships between local agro-dealers and national seed producers, supports group purchases of seeds and inputs, and disseminates technical information through demonstrations and printed materials. Digital technologies are leveraged to enhance seed marketing and facilitate purchases by smallholder farmers.
Third, AFDP promotes farmer awareness and demand for improved seeds. It aims to reach 200,000 households across 40 districts in 10 regions, focusing on maize, sunflower, and pulses. Through farmer field schools, on-farm demonstrations, seed fairs, and nutrition education, the programme introduces farmers to new technologies and best practices. It also empowers local farmer organizations to provide advisory services and uses digital platforms to disseminate information. Financial services are facilitated to support input purchases.
Finally, the programme strengthens market linkages by fostering partnerships between farmers and agribusinesses. It encourages contract farming and pricing agreements with processors, connects farmers to structured trading platforms like G-Soko, and conducts market mapping studies. Support is also provided to youth entrepreneurs and cooperatives, and technical and business information is widely shared. AFDP collaborates with existing initiatives such as the Agricultural Market Development Trust (AMDT) and the Pan African Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) to maximize impact and promote best practices.

ii) The AFDP programme’s fish market development and value addition component focuses on reducing postharvest losses and increasing income opportunities, particularly for women and youth. It aims to improve infrastructure and introduce technologies that enhance the quality and marketability of fish products. These investments are expected to benefit over 30,000 artisanal fishers, processors, and traders, while creating direct and indirect employment for around 1,000 youth along the tuna value chain.
To achieve this, the programme will co-finance the establishment of eight ice-making plants, three cold chain and processing facilities, ten solar dryers for seaweed and small pelagic fish (dagaa), and 80 dagaa drying racks. Additionally, modern fish markets will be rehabilitated in Pangani and Bagamoyo, modeled after successful markets in Dar es Salaam. These facilities will be managed by cooperatives and small enterprises, with sustainable user-fee systems to ensure proper maintenance and long-term viability.
AFDP will also support access to finance for fishers’ cooperatives and associations through partnerships with financial institutions, facilitated by the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB). This will enable investment in equipment, infrastructure, and working capital, with a focus on youth and women-led groups.
In aquaculture, the programme will strengthen farmer clusters and link them with private hatcheries. It will establish aquaculture field schools to train youth and women, promote collective marketing, and improve access to inputs and cold storage. These clusters will coordinate production to ensure a steady supply of fish and engage in local governance and policy advocacy.
For the seaweed sector, which is predominantly female-led, AFDP will address challenges in processing and value addition. It will fund market analyses, strengthen cooperatives, and provide equipment such as drying racks, solar dryers, milling machines, and packaging materials. The programme will also support the development of seaweed-based small enterprises and link them to financial and business services. Partnerships with organizations like The Nature Conservancy and buyers such as Cargill will help scale market access and improve product quality. An inclusive business model from Zanzibar will be adapted to Pemba and mainland Tanzania to promote fair pricing, compliance with standards, and collective bargaining.

planEntities.description: This project aims to raise awareness and capacity building of MDAs, workers' and employers' organisations and other stakeholders on Convention 190 to address issues of violence and harassment. Violence and harassment is a daily reality especially for large number of women and children. In Tanzania its prevalence is high hence addressing it, is a central development goal in its own right and key to achieving other development outcomes for women, their families, communities and the nation. Violence also affects negatively on economic growth and on poverty reduction initiatives. Discrimination, gender based violence and violence against women are critical bottleneck in achieving National Development Goals. Violence prevents the Tanzanian economy from attaining its full economic potential as it is diverting resources from their optimal use and it has significant negative impact on attaining of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030, African Agenda 2063 - The Africa We Want, and the Tanzania Development Vision 2025 which target high quality livelihood, good governance and the rule of law.

planEntities.description: This project focuses on providing technical and financial support to employers and trade unions to build their capacity on collective bargaining for the purpose of reaching agreements and concluding CBAs that promote ending of harassment and violence against women at work places. in negotiating such CBAs special emphasis should be placed on the role of international labour standards, especially Convention 190 and other relevant standards, in ending all forms of violence and harassment at work. The CBAs to be concluded should recognize the words enshrined in Convention 190 that it is the right of everyone to a world of work free from violence and harassment, including gender-based violence and harassment, and that violence and harassment in the world of work can constitute a human rights violation or abuse, and that violence and harassment is a threat to equal opportunities, is unacceptable and incompatible with decent work. It is for these reasons that the Convention promotes the importance of a work culture based on mutual respect and dignity of the human being to prevent violence and harassment.

planEntities.description: UN Joint Program on Unpaid care, disability and Gender Transformative Approach is part of a global joint programme funded by the Global Disability Fund and implemented by six UN agencies: UNDP, UN Women, UNICEF, UNFPA, ILO, and OHCHR. Spanning Tanzania, Mozambique, Kenya, Colombia, and Panama, it aims to foster an intersectional approach to care system reforms. The programme seeks to understand and dismantle the multiple barriers faced by women and girls, including those with disabilities, in achieving economic justice and accessing necessary inclusive services. While striving for joint ambitions and common outcomes, the programme is tailored and adapted to fit the national contexts and unique characteristics of each country. In Tanzania it is implemented by UNDP, UN Women and UNFPA.

planEntities.description:
The specific objectives of the programme (SWITCH Africa Green Phase II) are to support the development of green businesses, eco-entrepreneurship and promote the use of SCP practices by having in place:
1. Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) and business service providers that are better equipped to
seize opportunities for green business development, 
2. Better informed producers and consumers, and
3. Enabling conditions inclusive of clear policies, sound regulatory instruments, incentives structures (including
tax, other fiscal and market-based instruments) influencing key sector(s) in the six African countries.

planEntities.name: Demonstrate the financial and economic viability of clean energy captive installations for industries in pilot commercial sites in key industries
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1 Institutional capacities of National and sub-national Government strengthened to facilitate a Just Transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy/society
planEntities.description:
The Clean Captive Installations for Industrial Clients in Sub-Sahara Africa (South Africa, Ghana, Kenya and Nigeria)  aims to strengthen the ability of the four identified countries – Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa – to move towards low carbon-emitting development strategies in order to have sustainable development and overall human well-being. It also contributes to several Sustainable Development Goals, including
Climate Action (SDG 13),
Responsible Consumption and Production (SDG 12),
Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG 7), and
Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure (SDG 9).
Components
Component 1: Baseline studies and awareness raising
Component 2: Economic and financial tools and assessments
Component 3: Realization of one pilot project per country
Component 4: Knowledge dissemination and outreach

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
planEntities.description: This will be achieved through the the project "The Life Cycle Initiative: enabling global use of life cycle knowledge to support decision making for Sustainable Consumption and Production" that links experts and users (policy- and decision-makers) in dialogue platforms to enhance their understanding; this is enabled by the internal links with UN Environment hosted projects, initiatives and secretariats, which adapt to country and regional specificities. The project also builds on the strength of the Life Cycle Initiative in the capacity development area that delivers such capacity on the ground. And third, substantive intervention is targeted at continuing to strengthen the consensus building around accessibility and interoperability of life cycle knowledge as a foundation of life cycle approaches.

planEntities.name: Provide adequate education and training such that future professionals can succeed in an increasingly resource constrained world
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1 Institutional capacities of National and sub-national Government strengthened to facilitate a Just Transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy/society
planEntities.description: Under the Environmental Education and Youth Project two key areas will focused on to achieve the required outputs : (1) Developing the capacity of future professionals and education institutions; supporting the engagement of universities in achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals; and (2) Scaling up action under partnerships on education for sustainable development. The first area encompasses the development and dissemination of education material as well as changes in curricula within targeted education institutions (primarily higher education but partnering for curricula change at other levels as appropriate).

planEntities.name: Promotion and Delivery of Environmentally Sound Waste Management Technologies and Methods and in-Country Technical and Advisory Support
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
planEntities.description: The activities for Promotion and Delivery of Environmentally Sound Waste Management Technologies and Methods and in-Country Technical and Advisory Support include development of policies and legal instruments, institutional and fiscal strategies and mechanisms for waste prevention and sound management developed or implemented in countries within the framework of relevant multilateral environmental agreements and SAICM

planEntities.name: Strengthen science-based policymaking for increased impact towards the SDGs by assessing key environmental issues and providing focused outlooks
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1 Institutional capacities of National and sub-national Government strengthened to facilitate a Just Transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy/society
planEntities.description: Assessing key environmental issues and providing focused outlooks to strengthen science-based policy and decision making aims to identify environmental challenges and opportunities for sustainable development, while strengthening the science-policy interface to support regional, national and local governments, the business sector, and civil society including non-governmental organizations and local community groups (women, men and children). The project’s approach will be integrated, inclusive and evidence-based, ensuring scientific robustness and credibility, policy-neutral legitimacy and enhanced transparency.

planEntities.name: Strengthen responses to land-based pollution of the marine environment and address related issues of concern identified by governments
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
planEntities.description: This will strengthen responses to land-based pollution of the marine environment and address related issues of concern identified by governments under "Protecting the Marine Environment from Land-Based Pollution through Coordinated and Strengthened Global Action" project. This will also includes strengthening of co-operation around the prevention of land-based pollution by fostering action targeting the sources of marine litter, nutrients and wastewater pollution.

planEntities.name: Enhance capacities of Parties to the Chemicals and Waste MEAs, in particular the Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm and Minamata Conventions
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
planEntities.description: To achieve sound management of chemicals and waste worldwide, MEAs including the Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm and Minamata Conventions, and SAICM have been established to address specific chemicals and waste through international cooperative actions through the "5.III. Accelerating the implementation of the chemicals and waste Multilateral Environmental Agreements and achieving the targets of related Sustainable Development Goals for improved human health and a clean environment" project

planEntities.name: Support countries to reduce short-lived climate pollutants (SLCPs)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
planEntities.description: Supporting countries is done through Climate and Clean Air Coalition to Reduce Short-Lived Climate Pollutants ("the Coalition”) project. The outcomes are obtained by: (1) raising awareness of SLCP impacts and mitigation strategies; (2) enhancing and developing new national and regional actions, including by identifying and overcoming barriers, enhancing capacity, and mobilizing support; (3) promoting best practices and showcasing successful efforts; and (4) improving scientific understanding of SLCP impacts and mitigation strategies. UNEP hosts the Coalition’s Secretariat in Paris, manages its Trust Fund and will implement an array of actions funded by the Coalition.

planEntities.name: Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2.1 Strenghtened capacity of national and sub-national institutions to sustainably and efficiently manage Natural Resources
planEntities.description: The international community through the UN member states adopted, in September 2015, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development with 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among these SDGs, Goal 15 is particularly relevant for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Through this goal, countries are urged to, Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss. The target 15.3 urges countries to combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive to achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.

planEntities.name: Improving Access to COVID-19 Vaccinations for Vulnerable Migrants in Humanitarian Settings
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Capacities of national systems including domestic financial capacity and institutions to deliver human rights-based, people centered, comprehensive essential social services and protection systems for all are enhanced.
planEntities.description: In agreement with national governments, Ministries of Health, and international prioritization standards such as SAGE, IOM promoted equitable access to COVID‑19 vaccines for vulnerable populations in humanitarian settings through a wide range of targeted activities. Implemented by IOM Headquarters in Geneva with SDC funding, the project supported 38 countries from July 2021 to March 2022 to expand vaccination access for high‑risk and underserved groups—including migrants, refugees, IDPs, and other populations often excluded from national immunization plans. Through close coordination with Gavi, WHO, UNICEF, Ministries of Health and global COVID‑19 response platforms, the initiative strengthened vaccination delivery systems, improved micro‑planning and outreach, and enhanced last‑mile delivery capacities in complex humanitarian contexts. Guided by IOM’s global COVID‑19 SRRP, the project further improved country‑level preparedness, risk communication, and operational readiness to reduce infection rates and ensure the inclusion of mobile and marginalized populations. Across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, this collective effort contributed to broader global health security by advancing equitable access to life‑saving COVID‑19 vaccines for those most at risk.

planEntities.description:
"The landfall of Tropical Cyclone Eloise in the night of 23 January 2021 and previously, the Tropical Storm Chalane on 30 December 2020, have deeply affected areas in Central Mozambique. While the initial response has kickstarted, there is an urgent need to scale up in the areas of Shelter/NFI, CCCM, Protection/MHPSS and DTM to ensure adequate response to the needs of those affected by Tropical Cyclone Eloise in Central Mozambique trough sound, safe and integrated measures in resettlement locations for those who cannot return home. Building directly on its existing field presence and structures, with added value and comparative advantage on the response, IOM proposes to respond to the immediate humanitarian needs by providing emergency humanitarian assistance using a multisectoral and people-centered approach, increasing local capacity and (human) resources focusing on the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: Affected populations have safe and sustainable settlements through multisector integrated approaches to address disaster displacement
Outcome 2: Informed humanitarian and resilient response through the evidence-based assessments to inform the response

planEntities.name: Assessing COVID-19's Impact on Mixed Migration Flows: Trafficking in Persons, Smuggling of Migrants, and Related Protection Risks in Malawi, Mozambique and Zimbabwe
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Policies, strategies, laws and regulations for the use of environmental & natural resources, climate and disaster resilience are developed and strengthened based on good practices and standards and are gender transformative and include the needs of refugees and IDPs.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of  this project, is  to contribute to strengthening of protection measures and national responses to trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants. This includes specific impacts on women, children and youth, as well as the evolving routes, stakeholders, modus operandi, as well as needs and vulnerabilities of migrant populations of focus . The proposed project aims to conduct field research in areas of high irregular migration movements and other identified hotspots for data collection pertinent to the smuggling and trafficking of migrants. The research will be qualitative and rely on the collection of primary data through direct interviews with  a variety of governmental and  non-governmental stakeholders and key informants, as well as direct field assessments to be conducted by the research team in collaboration with the relevant national authorities. The findings will inform follow up awareness raising activities, intended to both inform identified populations about the risks of trafficking and smuggling post-COVID as well as through political level advocacy aimed at facilitating the adaptation of policy and programming responses by government stakeholders. Capacity building activities will also be developed to strengthen the capacity of relevant stakeholders towards managing migration flows post-COVID.

planEntities.name: Preventing Violent Extremism and Building Social Cohesion in the Northern Region of Mozambique, II

planEntities.description:
The project aims to build resilience to violent extremist influences in the Northern Region of Mozambique by understanding and addressing socio-economic needs in affected communities. Consistent with IOM’s Community Resilience and Peacebuilding (CRP) strategic approach, the project will build resilience and increase stability through programming addressing drivers of violent extremism in three outcomes:

1.       Empowered community members, particularly youth, contribute productively to households, communities and society

2.       Communities have stronger connections to, and more positive perceptions of, the government

3.       Social cohesion is increased as a protective factor against VE, and to promote stability

planEntities.name: Community Stabilization for Conflict-Affected Communities in Northern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: More people, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized and those affected by conflict, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to actively participate in and lead conflict prevention, community-led stabilization, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and recovery initiatives
planEntities.description:
This project will contribute to promoting community stabilization and preventing violent extremism in Northern Mozambique, particularly in communities affected by conflict with a specific focus on youth, women and girls.

In pursuit of this objective, IOM will initiate activities to support community-led conflict prevention and creating a conducive environment for communities to live peaceful and productive lives through income generation, school-based peace clubs, community-based projects prioritized by communities and support to the Government of Mozambique to discuss mechanisms and frameworks for reintegration of former and eligible non-state armed group (NSAG) members. By focusing on addressing root causes in a context-specific way, IOM aims to promote stability, reduce vulnerability and build local resilience - contributing to Mozambique achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions.

planEntities.name: Humanitarian Response in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique (Phase III)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: More people, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized and those affected by conflict, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to actively participate in and lead conflict prevention, community-led stabilization, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and recovery initiatives
planEntities.description:
In response to the acute needs of displaced and vulnerable migrants in Cabo Delgado, IOM is currently implementing a comprehensive and integrated Health, WASH, CCCM, DTM, MHPSS, and Shelter intervention. The overall objective of the ongoing project is to ensure dignified, safe, and secure living conditions and access to essential services for populations affected by disasters driven by natural hazards and conflict, while contributing to empowered and resilient individuals and communities across northern Mozambique. This intervention forms part of IOM’s broader multi-donor, multisectoral humanitarian response in the region, which has reached an estimated 784,319 IDPs as of February 2022.

The project is being implemented within the framework of the Humanitarian–Development–Peace Nexus (HDPN), aimed at reducing overall vulnerability, decreasing unmet needs, strengthening risk management capacities, and addressing the root causes of fragility and displacement. Through this integrated approach, the project simultaneously responds to urgent humanitarian needs while supporting recovery, resilience-building, and pathways toward durable solutions. Please note that while the project is operational until March 2027, for the purposes of the current CF submission, the end date will be set as 31 March 2026

planEntities.description: The Local Climate Adaptive Living Facility (LoCAL)  was designed to provide solutions and access to climate finance for Mozambican local governments in 2014. Since then, with generous support from Belgium, Sweden, Switzerland, the European Union and the Region of Catalonia, around 100 adaptive development infrastructures have been financed in 54 of the 154 districts in Mozambique during the implementation of the LoCAL Mechanism. To date, LoCAL has directly benefited approximately three million people in the country - almost 10% of the Mozambican population - and channeled approximately US$25 million directly to local governments in Mozambique.

planEntities.description: MERCIM uses UNCDF methodologies that strengthen the capacity of local governments to improve the delivery of basic climate-resilient services to communities and to enhance decision-making processes based on local knowledge. This means providing training and technical assistance to governments so that communities can genuinely participate in planning, budgeting and other local governance processes. MERCIM channels, through the national public finance management system, climate finance to local government authorities for locally-led adaptation, using Performance-Based Climate Resilience Grants. These grants provide additional decentralized resources to finance local climate-resilient investments. The annual performance of local authorities determines their budget allocation for the following year.

planEntities.description: The DELPAZ program was launched in October 2021 as part of the European Union's support for the implementation of the Maputo Accord for Peace and National Reconciliation. Under the leadership of the Government of Mozambique with support from the Austrian Development Agency, the Italian Development Cooperation Agency and the United Nations Capital Development Fund, DELPAZ aims to promote local economic development opportunities in communities previously affected by conflict in 14 districts of Sofala, Provinces of Manica and Tete. UNCDF's role in DELPAZ is to support authorities in strengthening the inclusion of local voices in planning and budgeting exercises, as a solid foundation for promoting lasting peace, national reconciliation and inclusive sustainable development.

planEntities.name: Informal Economy Project
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Legal frameworks targeting productive capacity, competitiveness, infrastructure, trade and investment, information and communications are strengthened, gender sensitive and include the needs of refugees and IDPs, and new digital technologies are inclusive and more accessible.
planEntities.description:
The project will strengthen informal firms' ecosystem, and increase their ability and willingness for growth and formalization.
The expected outcome of the project is to support and enable informal enterprises transition towards sustainable growth and formalization in Mozambique. 
The main objective of the project is to facilitate informal firms’ growth and formalization in the following four main results areas:
(1)	Create an enabling regulatory environment for informal enterprises through the promotion of an integrated policy framework for the formalization of informal enterprises in Mozambique; 
(2)	Facilitate access to finance through the development and promotion of new financial services, and the expansion of capitalization opportunities for financial intermediaries;
(3)	Build capacity among informal economy intermediaries and informal enterprises and promote digital finance technology use.
(4)	Foster collective and mutually reinforcing action and innovations to address gaps in selected sectors through the establishment and operationalization of an agricultural commercialization sector collective action platform. This platform will contribute to identifying and addressing systemic gaps in this particular sector of the Mozambican economy.

planEntities.name: Support  the implementation of the Management Plan of the UNESCO Quirimbas Biophere Reserve (QBR)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: Government institutions have stronger capacities for evidence-based (including gender analysis) decision making, accountability, and effective coordination for disasters and climate resilience, resilient infrastructures and the sustainable management of environment and natural resources ;
planEntities.description: The QBR has great ecological and economic value, but faces a number of challenges such as deforestation, poaching, illegal mining, hunting, overfishing, and over-exploitation of livelihoods. These combined pressures negatively impact biodiversity and resource conservation, and the livelihoods of vulnerable local communities. In this context, the management plan being developed through the MAPQUIBO project aims to frame priority areas for action in the years ahead, and after its approval, its operationalization is required. Biodiversity conservation, environmental education, research, and sustainable development are key elements in promoting the harmonious integration of people and nature in biosphere reserves. In particular, both ESD and disaster risk reduction (DRR) are relevant in a context where poverty and vulnerability to climate change and natural disasters are prevalent and where innovative solutions for sustainable development are needed.

planEntities.name: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL RESILIENT RECOVERY OF THE IBO & BUZI DISTRICT: Supporting reconstruction of local authorities and communities in a context of environmental and cultural heritage and sensitivity.

planEntities.description: Cyclone Kenneth caused significant damage in Northern Mozambique, after its landfall on April 25th 2019. The Post Disaster Housing Action Plan (PALPOC), promoted by the Reconstruction Cabinet as tool to orientate the resilient reconstruction of settlements and houses, targets as a priority for this region the Districts of Macomia, Ibo and Quissanga as the most affected. All of them are situated along the cost of the Quirimbas National Park. This project funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), as part of the reconstruction contribution, pledged in Beira Donors Conference on May 2nd, focuses mainly on Ibo District, including Ibo, Quirimbas and Matemo Islands, where around 90% of the housing stock was severely affected or totally destroyed, together with the majority of livelihoods means and public infrastructure, leaving the community in a level of extreme vulnerability.

planEntities.name: By 2026, girls, boys and adolescents, and their families and communities have increased knowledge and awareness and are better equipped to prevent violence and harmful practices
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1: Mechanisms and capacities of community actors and institutions, including in refugee and IDP hosting areas, to address discriminatory gender and social cultural norms, and prevent and respond to violence and harmful practices are strengthened.
planEntities.description: Harmful social norms continue to take a heavy toll on child protection efforts in Mozambique. The prevention of violence through the promotion of positive social norms and behaviour change is a slow process that requires long term commitment and steady engagement with a wide range of partners and with communities, families, adolescents and children. The implementation of the VAC school-based referral mechanism is a landmark achievement and the roll-out of the operational plan to implement the mechanism will be a priority in the new Country Programme, working across sectors, under the leadership of the Education team.  Work with C4D, will focus on triggering behavioural change with and within communities, addressing harmful effects of social (and negative gender) norms and practices that act as socio-cultural barriers towards positive social change. Initiatives will aim to break the culture of silence that continue to hamper reporting and denunciation of acts of violence committed against children, including child marriage. A wide range of Communication for Development methodologies and tools will be developed and used to ensure a multi-level, multi-sectoral, participatory and inclusive social change process, using gender-transformative approaches to ensure gender differences and inequalities are addressed. Activities for prevention of violence and harmful practices will comprise of two inter-connected pillars: social behaviour change communication and parenting skills. Close collaboration  with social protection will ensure that vulnerable children and families do not fall through the social safety.

planEntities.description: While Mozambique has made significant strides in establishing a progressive legal framework and policies that conform with core international standards, there are a number of gaps that have prevented implementation, including the need for additional regulations, standards and guidelines. In particular, there is a lack of reliable systematic administrative data on child protection and insufficient overall investment in child protection. Efforts are needed in the collection of data to inform prevention and response to violence against children. There is also a need to invest at national and subnational levels in budget review and introduce a child-rights perspective into the budgeting process with clear allocations and specific indicators for children in the relevant sectors and agencies, combined with a tracking system to monitor and evaluate the adequacy, efficacy and equitability of the distribution of resources allocated for child protection priorities.

planEntities.name: Towards sustainable energy for all: Promoting market-based dissemination of integrated renewable energy systems for productive activities in rural areas
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3 The primary sector is more sustainable, productive, value-adding and inclusive of forcibly displaced persons and incorporating circular, regenerative and gender transformative practices.
planEntities.description:
1. Project background information 
In Mozambique, the rural electrification rate reached only 27% as the extension of electricity grids has proven to be technically difficult, very costly and sometimes an inefficient solution due to the remoteness and sparse population density. The agricultural sector -one of the most important sectors of the economy- faces serious challenges in accessing electricity and other forms of modern energy forcing it to rely on expensive diesel, firewood and/or charcoal for its operations. Even though it has been estimated that Mozambique has a potential of 7 GW on renewable projects, the use of modern energy for productive uses is still very limited. As such, the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) –as an implementing agency of the Global Environment Facility (GEF)- and the Government of Mozambique are implementing the project “Towards sustainable energy for all in Mozambique: Promoting market-based dissemination of integrated renewable energy systems for productive activities in rural areas” which seeks –among other outcomes– to demonstrate the technical feasibility and commercial viability of renewables in productive sectors including agriculture and agro-food processing industries.

2. Project objective and description 
Through its 3 technical components, the project will support the market-based adoption of integrated renewable energy (RE) systems (solar PV for irrigation and waste-to-energy) in small to medium-scale farms and rural agro-food processing industries in Mozambique. The components are the following: 
1.	Establishment of a conducive policy and regulatory environment - the project will enhance the regulatory and policy environment to promote the involvement of the private sector in the development of integrated RE systems for rural areas. 
2.	Capacity building and knowledge management- the project will improve and develop the capabilities and knowledge of market players and enablers in the RE sector including relevant government officials (national and provincial level) as well as representatives from financial institutions, private sector, universities, and vocational training institutions. 
3.	Technology demonstration and scaling up - the project will demonstrate the technical and financial feasibility of RE technologies in agricultural activities located in rural areas, specifically: solar PV water pumping and biogas/biomass usage in agro-food processing industries through the installation of demonstration projects. The objectives of these projects, besides delivering GHG emission reductions, include generating case studies and best practices on the use of RE technologies in agro-food processing industries that have high replication potential across Mozambique. In this regard, UNIDO/GEF is offering a grant to support these demonstration projects in rural Mozambique to mitigate the high up-front costs required for such investment projects.

planEntities.name: UNIDO - FAO Opportunities for Youth in Africa (OYA): Accelerating job creation in agriculture and agribusiness
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.2 L’environnement des affaires est efficient, inclusif et transparent, et favorise l’initiative privée, une meilleure productivité et compétitivité ainsi que l’employabilité
planEntities.description: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) developed this joint programme in response to a dedicated call for accelerating efforts in the area of job creation for African youth, especially through agribusiness and entrepreneurship development.This call was made during the 2018 Conference on Youth Employment in Agriculture co-organized by the African Union, the Government of Rwanda and FAO, which took place on 20-21 August 2018 in Kigali, Rwanda, with the theme: “Youth Employment in Agriculture as a Solid Solution to Ending Hunger and Poverty in Africa: Engaging through Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) and Entrepreneurship”. This programme proposes an integrated approach for the creation of quality on- and off farm employment and self-employment opportunities for African youth in agriculture and agribusiness. It highlights the central role of agriculture for Africa’s development, while emphasizing the need for continuous empowerment of African youth to be the engine of this growth. The multi-level approach (continental, sub-regional, national) reflects the need for a concerted effort between public institutions and the private sector on capacity development, access to resources, improved coordination and linkages, and knowledge generation and dissemination. This programme provides an opportunity to strengthen the collaboration between FAO and UNIDO, and to position both agencies jointly on decent rural employment creation, agribusiness and value chain development, and support to small- and medium-enterprises (SMEs) in agriculture. By coming together, FAO and UNIDO will leverage on their strengths as knowledge organizations as well as technical agencies with extensive experience on decent employment creation and entrepreneurship development.
